profileDesc.creation:
Initially created: 2025-11-23T03:52:02.949+09:00 by CH Translate the following text from Classical Chinese into $lang.
Requirements: 1. The text contains page numbers in square brackets, such as [01], [02], etc. - These must be passed through unchanged. - Each page number must appear in exactly the same position in the translation as in the source. - The number of page markers in the output must match the input exactly.
2. Personal names, place names, titles, and other proper nouns should be rendered in Hànyǔ Pīnyīn with tone marks.
3. Do NOT transcribe the full Classical Chinese text into Pinyin.
4. Do NOT include explanatory notes, annotations, or commentary — output only the $lang translation.
5. The target language is $lang.
Input text:

p.seg: First year, spring, the king's first month.
What is meant by "first year"?
It is the first year of the ruler's reign.
What is meant by "spring"?
It is the beginning of the year.
Who is referred to by "king"?
It refers to King Wén.
Why is "king" mentioned before "first month"?
It is the king's first month.
Why mention the king's first month?
To emphasize the great unity.
Why is it not stated that the duke ascended the throne?
To fulfill the duke's intention.
How does it fulfill the duke's intention?
The duke intended to pacify the state and return it to Huán.
Why return it to Huán?
Huán was young but noble,
while Yǐn was older but of lower status.
The distinction between their noble and low status was subtle,
and the people of the state were unaware of it.
Yǐn was older and also virtuous,
so the various great officers supported Yǐn and established him.
If Yǐn had then declined the establishment,
it would have been uncertain whether Huán would necessarily be established.
Moreover, if Huán were established,
Yǐn feared that the great officers might not be able to assist a young ruler,
thus Yǐn's establishment was ultimately for Huán's establishment.
Yǐn was older and virtuous;
why was it not appropriate to establish him?
The heir is established based on seniority, not virtue;
a son is established based on nobility, not seniority.
Why was Huán noble?
Because his mother was noble.
If the mother is noble, why is the son noble?
The son is noble because of the mother;
the mother is noble because of the son.
In the third month,
the duke and Zhūlóu Yífù made a covenant at Mò.
What is meant by "and"?
It means "with."
Both "meet" and "and" mean "with."
Why is it sometimes said "meet,"
sometimes "and,"
and sometimes "jointly"?
"Meet" implies gathering;
"and" implies eagerness;
"jointly" implies reluctance.
"And" indicates our desire for it;
"jointly" indicates it was unavoidable.
Who is Yífù?
He is the ruler of Zhūlóu.
Why is he referred to by his personal name?
It is his courtesy name.
Why is his courtesy name used?
To praise him.
Why praise him?
Because he made a covenant with the duke.
Many made covenants with the duke;
why is he alone praised here?
Because he was worthy of praise and thus praised.
How was he worthy of praise?
He progressed gradually.
What is Mò?
It is the place of the meeting.
In summer, the fifth month,
the Earl of Zhèng defeated Duàn at Yān.
What is meant by "defeated"?
It means killed him.
If he killed him, why say "defeated"?
To magnify the wickedness of the Earl of Zhèng.
Why magnify his wickedness?
His mother wished to establish Duàn,
yet he killed him;
it would have been better not to grant him anything at all.
Who is Duàn?
He is the younger brother of the Earl of Zhèng.
Why is he not called "younger brother"?
Because he acted as the ruler of the state.
Why mention the place?
Because he acted as the ruler.
Why was the place not mentioned when the men of Qí killed Wúzhī?
Because it happened within the state.
If it happens within the state, even if one acts as ruler, the place is not mentioned;
if one does not act as ruler, even if it happens outside, the place is also not mentioned.
In autumn, the seventh month,
the Heavenly King sent Minister Xuǎn to come and present the funeral gifts for Huì Gōng and Zhòngzǐ.
What is a "minister"?
It is an official.
Who is Xuǎn?
It is his personal name.
Why is he referred to by his official title?
He was a minister-official.
Who is Huì Gōng?
He is Yǐn's deceased father.
Who is Zhòngzǐ?
She is Huán's mother.
Why is she not called "lady"?
Because Huán had not yet become ruler.
What are funeral gifts?
There are funeral gifts for mourning affairs.
Funeral gifts include horses, teams of horses, and bolts of silk;
carriages and horses are called "fèng,"
goods and wealth are called "fù,"
clothing and coverings are called "suì."
If Huán had not yet become ruler, why did the feudal lords come to present funeral gifts?
Because Yǐn was established for Huán,
so he announced the mourning for Huán's mother to the feudal lords.
Then why is this recorded?
To fulfill the duke's intention.
Why does it say "come"?
Because it was not in time for the event.
Why does it mention Huì Gōng and Zhòngzǐ together?
They were combined.
Combining them was contrary to ritual.
Why does it not say "and Zhòngzǐ"?
Because Zhòngzǐ was of low status.
In the ninth month,
a covenant was made with men of Sòng at Sù.
Who made it with them?
It was an insignificant person from our state.
In winter, the twelfth month,
Zhài Bó came.
Who is Zhài Bó?
He is a great officer of the Son of Heaven.
Why is it not stated that he was sent?
Because he was fleeing.
If he was fleeing, why not say "fled"?
Because the king has no outside;
to say "fled" would imply there is an outside.
Gōngzǐ Yìshī died.
Why is the day not recorded?
Because it was long ago.
What was seen is recorded differently;
what was heard is recorded differently;
what was transmitted is recorded differently.
Second year, spring,
the duke met with the Róng at Qián.
Summer, fifth month,
men of Jǔ entered Xiàng.
What is meant by "entered"?
It means they obtained it but did not occupy it.
Wúhài led troops and entered Jí.
Who is Wúhài?
He is Zhǎn Wúhài.
Why is his clan name not used?
To贬 demote him.
Why贬 demote him?
To express disapproval of the beginning of annihilation.
Did annihilation begin here?
It had occurred before this.
If it occurred before, why start here?
It is a recorded beginning.
Why record the beginning here?
Because it is the beginning of the Chūnqiū.
This was an annihilation;
why does it say "entered"?
For great evils within, they are concealed.
Autumn, eighth month, on Gēngchén,
the duke and the Róng made a covenant at Táng.
In the ninth month,
Jì Lǚxū came to escort the bride.
Who was Jì Lǚxū?
He was a senior official of Jì.
Why is he not referred to as an envoy?
In matrimonial rites, the principal is not named.
Then how should one refer?
Refer to the father, elder brothers, teachers, or friends.
When Duke Sòng sent Gōngsūn Shòu to present betrothal gifts,
why then was the principal named?
Because the wording was exhausted.
What does "the wording was exhausted" mean?
It means there was no mother.
Then did Jì have a mother?
It is said: Yes.
If there was one, why was the mother not named?
Because the mother did not communicate.
Escorting a bride from another state is not recorded,
why is this recorded?
To criticize.
What is criticized here?
Criticizing the beginning of not personally escorting the bride.
Did the practice of not personally escorting begin here?
It existed before this.
If it existed before, why does it begin here?
It is designated as the beginning.
Why designate it as the beginning?
Because it is the start of the Spring and Autumn Annals.
Why is a woman sometimes called "woman"?
Sometimes called "wife"?
Or sometimes called "lady"?
While in her own state, she is called "woman";
on the journey, she is called "wife";
upon entering the state, she is called "lady."
In winter, the tenth month,
Bó Jī went to Jì.
Who was Bó Jī?
She was a daughter of the Lǔ state.
Why does it say "went"?
For a woman, getting married is called "going."
Jì Zǐbó and the ruler of Jǔ made a covenant at Mì.
Who was Jì Zǐbó?
Nothing is heard about him.
In the twelfth month, on the yǐmǎo day,
Lady Zǐshì passed away.
Who was Lady Zǐshì?
She was the mother of Duke Yǐn.
Why is her burial not recorded?
To fulfill the duke's intention.
How does it fulfill the duke's intention?
The son would not ultimately act as ruler,
so the mother also did not ultimately act as lady.
The people of Zhèng attacked Wèi.
In the third year, spring, the royal second month, on the jǐsì day,
there was an eclipse of the sun.
Why is it recorded?
To record an anomaly.
Why are solar eclipses sometimes dated, sometimes not dated?
Sometimes the new moon is mentioned, sometimes not?
Saying "on such-and-such month, such-and-such day, the new moon,
there was an eclipse of the sun"
means the eclipse occurred exactly on the new moon.
If it is sometimes dated, sometimes not,
it is either ahead or behind.
Ahead means the new moon was earlier;
behind means the new moon was later.
In the third month, on the gēngxū day,
the Heavenly King passed away.
Why is his burial not recorded?
For the Son of Heaven, the passing is recorded but not the burial,
as it must occur at the proper time.
For feudal lords, both the death and burial are recorded,
because with the Son of Heaven existing,
they cannot ensure it occurs at the proper time.
Why is it sometimes said "bēng" and sometimes "hōng"?
For the Son of Heaven, it is "bēng";
for feudal lords, it is "hōng";
for senior officials, it is "zú";
for officers, it is "not receiving emolument."
In summer, the fourth month, on the xīnmǎo day,
Yǐnshì died.
Who was Yǐnshì?
He was a senior official of the Son of Heaven.
Why is he called Yǐnshì?
To贬.
Why贬?
To criticize hereditary ministers,
as hereditary ministers are contrary to ritual.
Deaths of senior officials from other states are not recorded,
why is this one recorded?
Because the Heavenly King had passed away, and he was the host for the feudal lords.
In autumn,
Wǔshìzǐ came to request funeral contributions.
Who was Wǔshìzǐ?
He was a senior official of the Son of Heaven.
Why is he called Wǔshìzǐ?
To criticize.
What is criticized here?
The father had died, and the son had not yet received a mandate.
Why is he not referred to as an envoy?
Because during mourning, he is not yet the ruler.
Why is Wǔshìzǐ coming to request funeral contributions recorded?
To criticize.
What is criticized here?
In mourning matters, one should not make requests;
requesting contributions is contrary to ritual,
and this applies to all below.
In the eighth month, on the gēngchén day,
Duke Sòng Hé died.
In winter, the twelfth month,
the Marquis of Qí and the Earl of Zhèng made a covenant at Shímén.
On the guǐwèi day,
Duke Sòng Mù was buried.
Why are burials sometimes dated, sometimes not dated?
If not timely and dated,
it is an urgent burial.
If not timely and not dated,
it is a negligent burial.
If overdue and dated,
it is concealed.
If overdue and not dated,
it is called being unable to bury.
If timely and not dated, it is correct.
If timely and dated, it indicates danger of not being buried.
Why was there danger at this timely burial?
Duke Xuān said to Duke Mù:
"In terms of my affection for you,
it is not as great as for Yǔyí.
But as the master of the state altars and ancestral temples,
Yǔyí is not as capable as you.
Why not ultimately become the ruler?"
After Duke Xuān died,
Duke Mù was established,
and Duke Mù exiled his two sons, Duke Zhuang Féng and Zuǒshī Bó,
saying:
"As my sons,
in life, do not see each other;
in death, do not mourn each other."
Yǔyí responded:
"The reason the former ruler did not give the state to me but handed it to you
was that you could be the master of the state altars and ancestral temples.
Now you are exiling your two sons and will give the state to me,
this is not the former ruler's intention.
Moreover, if a son can be exiled,
then the former ruler would have exiled me."
Duke Mù said:
"That the former ruler did not exile you is evident;
I stand here as regent."
He ultimately gave the state to Yǔyí.
Duke Zhuang Féng assassinated Yǔyí.
Therefore, the nobleman highly values correct succession.
The disaster of Sòng was caused by Duke Xuān.
In the fourth year, spring, the royal second month.
The people of Jǔ attacked Qǐ,
and took Móulóu.
What was Móulóu?
It was a town of Qǐ.
Taking towns from other states is not recorded,
why is this recorded?
To condemn the beginning of seizing towns.
On the wùshēn day,
Wèi Zhōuxū assassinated his ruler Wán.
Why is he referred to by the state name?
Because he controlled the state.
In summer,
the duke and the Duke of Sòng met at Qīng.
What does "met" mean?
It means unplanned.
One ruler went out,
and the other ruler intercepted him.
The Duke of Sòng, the Marquis of Chén, the people of Cài, and the people of Wèi attacked Zhèng.
In autumn,
Huī led troops to join Duke Sòng, Marquis Chén, men of Cài, and men of Wèi in attacking Zhèng.
Who is Huī?
It is Prince Huī.
Why is he not referred to as Prince?
To censure him.
Why is he censured?
Because he was involved in assassinating the Duke.
How was he involved in assassinating the Duke?
Prince Huī flattered Duke Yǐn,
saying to Duke Yǐn:
"The common people are content with you,
the feudal lords are pleased with you,
why not remain as ruler permanently?"
Duke Yǐn said:
"I will not;
I have ordered the repair of Túqiú,
and I plan to retire there."
Prince Huī feared that his words might be heard by Huán,
so he said to Huán:
"I have spoken on your behalf to Yǐn.
Yǐn said:
'I will not step down.'"
Huán said:
"Then what should be done?"
He replied:
"I request to start a revolt,
and assassinate Duke Yǐn."
It was during the Zhōng Wū sacrifice that Duke Yǐn was assassinated.
In the ninth month,
men of Wèi killed Zhōuyù at Pú.
Why are they referred to as 'men'?
It is the terminology for punishing a criminal.
In winter, the twelfth month,
men of Wèi established Jìn.
Who is Jìn?
It is Prince Jìn.
What does 'established' mean?
'Established' means it was improper to establish him.
Why are they referred to as 'men'?
It is the terminology for the multitude establishing him.
Then who established him?
Shí Què established him.
If Shí Què established him,
then why are they referred to as 'men'?
Because it was what the multitude desired to establish.
Although the multitude desired to establish him,
his establishment was improper.
In the fifth year, spring,
the Duke watched fish at Táng.
Why is this recorded?
To criticize.
Why criticize this?
Because it was distant.
Why did the Duke go far to watch fish?
To obtain them.
The Duke set traps for fish worth a hundred gold.
What does 'obtain them' mean?
It is terminology praising their size and beauty.
What is Táng?
It is a town on the Jì River.
In summer, the fourth month,
Duke Huán of Wèi was buried.
In autumn,
the army of Wèi entered Shèng.
Why is it sometimes said 'led troops' and sometimes not?
If the commander is noble and the army large, it is called 'so-and-so led troops';
if the commander is noble and the army small, it is called 'the commander';
if the commander is humble and the army large, it is called 'the army';
if the commander is humble and the army small, it is called 'men'.
For the ruler as commander, 'led troops' is not stated,
to record what is most significant.
In the ninth month,
the temple of Zhòngzǐ was inaugurated.
What does 'inaugurate the temple' mean?
'Inaugurate' means to enter the chamber,
beginning the sacrifice to Zhòngzǐ.
Since Huán had not yet become ruler, why sacrifice to Zhòngzǐ?
Because Yǐn was established for Huán,
so he sacrificed to Huán's mother.
Then why is it mentioned?
To fulfill the Duke's intention.
The first offering was made with six rows of feather dancers.
What does 'first' mean?
It means the beginning.
What are the six rows of feathers?
It is a dance.
Why is the first offering with six rows of feathers recorded?
To criticize.
Why criticize this?
To criticize the beginning of usurping the rites of the Dukes.
How was the six rows of feathers a usurpation?
The Son of Heaven has eight rows,
the Dukes have six,
the feudal lords have four.
Who are the Dukes?
Who are the feudal lords?
The Three Dukes of the Son of Heaven are called Duke,
the descendants of the former kings are called Duke,
the other large states are called Marquis,
the small states are called Bó, Zǐ, or Nán.
Who are the Three Dukes of the Son of Heaven?
They are the ministers of the Son of Heaven.
Why are there three ministers of the Son of Heaven?
East of Shǎn is overseen by the Duke of Zhōu,
west of Shǎn is overseen by the Duke of Shào,
and one minister remains at the court.
Did the usurpation of the Dukes' rites begin here?
It was before this.
If it was before this, why does it begin here?
Usurping the Dukes' rites can still be mentioned,
but usurping the Son of Heaven's rites cannot be mentioned.
Men of Zhūlóu and men of Zhèng attacked Sòng.
There were caterpillars.
Why is this recorded?
To record a disaster.
In winter, on the xīnsì day of the twelfth month,
Prince Kōu died.
Men of Sòng attacked Zhèng,
besieging Chánggé.
Towns are not usually said to be besieged,
why is it said here?
Because it was a stronghold.
In the sixth year, spring,
men of Zhèng came to deliver a peace agreement.
What does 'deliver a peace agreement' mean?
'Deliver a peace agreement' means to annul a settlement.
Why mention annulling a settlement?
Because their settlement was broken.
It is said, "Our settlement has failed."
We and the men of Zhèng had not reached a settlement.
Why had we and the men of Zhèng not reached a settlement?
Due to the battle of Húrǎng,
Duke Yǐn was captured there.
Then why is the battle not mentioned?
To conceal the capture.
In summer, on the xīnyǒu day of the fifth month,
the Duke met with the Marquis of Qí and made a covenant at Ài.
In autumn, the seventh month.
Why is this recorded when nothing happened?
Even if nothing happens, the Spring and Autumn Annals
records the beginning of each season when it passes.
Why record the beginning of each season when it passes?
The Spring and Autumn Annals is a chronicle;
all four seasons must be present to make a year.
In winter,
men of Sòng took Chánggé.
The taking of a town by another state is not usually recorded,
why is it recorded here?
Because it took a long time.
In the seventh year, spring, the royal third month,
Shū Jī went to Jì.
The Marquis of Téng died.
Why is his name not given?
Because it was a minor state.
If it was a minor state, why is he referred to as Marquis?
To avoid confusion.
The Spring and Autumn Annals does not avoid using the same title for noble and humble,
nor the same terminology for good and evil.
In summer,
the inner wall of Zhōngqiū was built.
What is Zhōngqiū?
It is a town within the state.
Why is the building of the inner wall of Zhōngqiū recorded?
It is recorded because it was important.
The Marquis of Qí sent his younger brother Nián on a friendly mission.
Why is he referred to as younger brother?
A younger brother by the same mother is called younger brother,
an elder brother by the same mother is called elder brother.
In autumn,
the Duke attacked Zhūlóu.
In winter,
the Heavenly King sent Fán Bó to conduct a diplomatic visit,
but the Róng people attacked Fán Bó at Chǔqiū,
and took him back with them.
Who was Fán Bó?
He was a senior official of the Son of Heaven.
This was a diplomatic mission,
so why is it described as an attack?
Because he was captured.
If he was captured, why use the term "attack"?
To magnify the event.
Why magnify it?
Because we do not approve of the barbarians capturing someone from the Central States.
Why mention the location?
To magnify the event.
In the eighth year, in spring,
the Duke of Sòng and the Marquis of Wèi met at Chuí.
In the third month,
the Earl of Zhèng sent Wǎn to come and hand over Bǐng.
Who was Wǎn?
He was a minor official of Zhèng.
What was Bǐng?
It was a bathing town of Zhèng.
When the Son of Heaven performed ceremonies at Tài Shān,
the feudal lords all accompanied him.
Below Tài Shān,
the feudal lords all had bathing towns there.
On the day Gēngyín,
we entered Bǐng.
Why is the term "enter" used?
Because it was difficult.
Why record the date?
Because it was difficult.
Why use the term "we"?
Using "we" indicates it was not only us,
but Qí also desired it.
In summer, in the sixth month, on the day Jǐhài,
the Marquis of Cài, Kǎofù, died.
On the day Xīnhài,
the Earl of Sù died.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the day Gēngwǔ,
the Duke of Sòng, the Marquis of Qí, and the Marquis of Wèi formed a covenant at Wǎwū.
In the eighth month,
the Duke of Cài, Xuān, was buried.
Why is the personal name used at death but not at burial?
Because the record of death follows the correct form,
while the burial follows the customs of the host state.
Why is the date recorded at death but not at burial?
Because the death is reported, but the burial is not announced.
In the ninth month, on the day Xīnmǎo,
the Duke and a person from Jǔ formed a covenant at Bāolái.
Why did the Duke form a covenant with a minor figure?
Referring to him as "a person" indicates that there was no doubt about following him.
There were crop-eating insects.
In winter, in the twelfth month,
Wúhài died.
This was Zhǎn Wúhài.
Why is his clan name not used?
Because they detested his beginning the destruction of states,
so throughout his life, his clan name was not used.
In the ninth year, in spring,
the Heavenly King sent Nán Jì to conduct a diplomatic visit.
In the third month, on the day Guǐyǒu,
there was heavy rain with thunder and lightning.
Why is this recorded?
To record an anomaly.
What was anomalous about it?
It was untimely.
On the day Gēngchén,
there was heavy snowfall.
Why is this recorded?
To record an anomaly.
What was anomalous about it?
It was extremely severe.
Xiá died.
Who was Xiá?
He was a senior official of ours who had not yet received a formal appointment.
In summer,
the city of Láng was walled.
In autumn, in the seventh month.
In winter,
the Duke met with the Marquis of Qí at Bǐng.
In the tenth year, in spring, in the royal second month,
the Duke met with the Marquis of Qí and the Earl of Zhèng at Zhōngqiū.
In summer,
Huī led troops to join the men of Qí and Zhèng in attacking Sòng.
This was Prince Huī,
so why is he not referred to as "Prince"?
To贬 demote him.
Why贬 demote him?
Because he was a criminal against Duke Yǐn.
Thus, throughout the chronicle of Duke Yǐn, he is贬 demoted.
In the sixth month, on the day Rénxū,
the Duke defeated the army of Sòng at Jiān.
On Xīnwèi, they took Gào;
on Xīnsì, they took Fáng.
When taking towns, dates are not usually recorded;
why are they recorded here?
Because they captured two places in one month.
Why mention capturing two in one month?
To emphasize the severity.
For major misdeeds within the state, they are concealed;
why emphasize the severity here?
The Spring and Autumn Annals records internal affairs in detail but external ones briefly;
for external major misdeeds, they are recorded,
but minor ones are not;
for internal major misdeeds, they are concealed,
while minor ones are recorded.
In autumn,
men of Sòng and Wèi entered Zhèng.
Men of Sòng, Cài, and Wèi attacked Zài,
and the Earl of Zhèng attacked and captured it.
Why say "attacked and captured it"?
Because it was easy.
How was it easy?
He relied on others' strength.
Whose strength did he rely on?
He relied on the strength of the men of Sòng, Cài, and Wèi.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the day Rénwǔ,
men of Qí and Zhèng entered Chéng.
In the eleventh year, in spring,
the Marquis of Téng and the Marquis of Xuē came for an audience.
Why use the term "audience"?
When feudal lords come, it is called an audience;
when senior officials come, it is called a visit.
Why mention them together?
Because they were minor states.
In summer, in the fifth month,
the Duke met with the Earl of Zhèng at Qílí.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the day Rénwǔ,
the Duke, along with the Marquis of Qí and the Earl of Zhèng, entered Xǔ.
In winter, in the eleventh month, on the day Rénchén,
the Duke passed away.
Why is the burial not recorded?
To conceal it.
What is concealed?
That he was assassinated.
If he was assassinated, why not record the burial?
In the Spring and Autumn Annals, if a ruler is assassinated and the perpetrator is not punished,
the burial is not recorded,
to indicate that there were no loyal ministers or sons.
Master Shěn Zǐ said:
"If a ruler is assassinated,
and the ministers do not punish the perpetrator,
they are not true ministers.
If a son does not avenge,
he is not a true son.
Burial is a matter for the living.
In the Spring and Autumn Annals, if a ruler is assassinated and the perpetrator is not punished,
the burial is not recorded,
to show that it is not connected to the ministers and sons.
Why is the place of the Duke's death not recorded?
Out of不忍言 unwillingness to speak of it.
Why is there no first month recorded for Duke Yǐn?
Because Duke Yǐn intended to yield to Huán,
so he did not claim the first month as his own."
In the first year, in spring, the king's first month,
the duke ascended the throne.
When succeeding a murdered ruler, it is not stated that he ascended the throne;
why is it stated here that he ascended the throne?
It was in accordance with his intention.
In the third month,
the duke met with the Earl of Zhèng at Chuí.
The Earl of Zhèng exchanged a jade disk for the fields of Xǔ.
Why does it say he exchanged it with a jade disk?
It was a swap.

Because it was dangerous.
Why dangerous?
Because we were duplicitous.
Lǔ Zǐ said:
"Our being duplicitous
was not because of them,
but because of us."
In the 24th year, in spring, the king's third month,
the pillars of Duke Huán's temple were carved.
Why is this recorded?
To criticize.
What is criticized here?
Carving the pillars of Duke Huán's temple was contrary to ritual.
We buried Duke Zhuāng of Cáo.
In summer,
the duke went to Qí to meet the bride.
Why is this recorded?
Personally going to meet the bride is in accordance with ritual.
In autumn,
the duke arrived from Qí.
On the dīngchǒu day of the eighth month,
Lady Jiāng entered.
Why does it say "entered"?
Because it was difficult.
Why is the date mentioned?
Because it was difficult.
How was it difficult?
The lady, not being submissive, could not be made to enter;
she made an agreement with the duke,
and only then did she enter.
On the wùyín day,
the great officers and the wives of the patrician families had an audience,
using silk.
Who are the wives of the patrician families?
They are the wives of the great officers.
What is an audience?
It is to be received in audience.
What about the use?
Using it means it should not be used.
Being received in audience using silk was contrary to ritual.
If so, then what should be used?
Dates and chestnuts, for instance,
or dried meat, for instance.
There was a great flood.
In winter,
the Róng invaded Cáo.
Cáo Jī fled to Chén.
Who was Cáo Jī?
He was a great officer of Cáo.
Cáo had no great officers,
why is this recorded?
Because he was worthy.
Why was Cáo Jī considered worthy?
When the Róng were about to invade Cáo,
Cáo Jī admonished, saying:
"The Róng are numerous and without righteousness;
I beg you, my lord, not to oppose them personally."
The Earl of Cáo said:
"It cannot be."
After three admonitions were not heeded,
he then left him;
therefore, the gentleman considered that he had grasped the righteousness between ruler and minister.
Chì returned to Cáo, to Lord Guō.
Who was Chì?
There was no one named Chì in Cáo;
it was probably Lord Guō.
Who was Lord Guō?
He was a ruler who had lost his land.
In the 25th year, in spring,
the Marquis of Chén sent Nǚshū to come on a friendly mission.
In summer, in the fifth month, on the guǐchǒu day,
the Marquis of Wèi, Shuò, died.
In the sixth month, on the xīnwèi day, the new moon,
there was an eclipse of the sun;
drums were beaten and victims were used at the altar of the soil.
Why, during a solar eclipse, were drums beaten and victims used at the altar of the soil?
It was to seek from the dark way;
they surrounded the altar of the soil with red silk,
some say to coerce it,
some say because it was dark,
fearing that people would offend it,
hence they surrounded it.
Bó Jī went to Qǐ.
In autumn,
there was a great flood;
drums were beaten and victims were used at the altar of the soil and at the gate.
Why does it say "at the altar of the soil and at the gate"?
At the altar of the soil was in accordance with ritual;
at the gate was contrary to ritual.
In winter,
the duke's son Yǒu went to Chén.
In the 26th year,
the duke attacked the Róng.
In summer,
the duke arrived from attacking the Róng.
Cáo put its great officers to death.
Why are their names not given?
Because they were many.
Why were they killed in multitude?
Because they did not die for the ruler of Cáo.
When a ruler dies in his position, it is called "annihilation";
why is it not said that he was annihilated?
It is to avoid the taboo for Cáo Jī.
This was probably a battle;
why is the battle not mentioned?
It is to avoid the taboo for Cáo Jī.
In autumn,
the duke joined with men of Sòng and Qí in attacking Xú.
In winter, in the twelfth month, on the guǐhài day, the new moon,
there was an eclipse of the sun.
In the 27th year, in spring,
the duke met with Bó Jī of Qǐ at Táo.
In summer, in the sixth month,
the duke met with the Marquis of Qí, the Duke of Sòng, the Marquis of Chén, and the Earl of Zhèng,
and they made a covenant at Yōu.
In autumn,
the duke's son Yǒu went to Chén,
to bury Yuán Zhòng.
Who was Yuán Zhòng?
He was a great officer of Chén.
The burial of a great officer is not recorded;
why is this recorded?
It is to make known the private journey of Jìzǐ.
Why make known Jìzǐ's private journey?
It was to avoid internal troubles.
A gentleman avoids internal troubles but does not avoid external troubles.
What were the internal troubles?
The duke's sons Qìngfù, Yá, and Yǒu were all full younger brothers of Duke Zhuāng.
Qìngfù and Yá had illicit relations with the lady to coerce the duke;
if Jìzǐ rose to deal with it,
he could not participate in the state's government;
if he sat and watched it, it was to cherish his kin.
Being unable to bear seeing it,
he therefore again requested to go to Chén to bury Yuán Zhòng.
In winter,
Bó Jī of Qǐ came.
Why does it say "came"?
Coming directly is called "coming";
returning for good is called "coming back."
Jǔ Qìng came to meet Shū Jī.
Who was Jǔ Qìng?
He was a great officer of Jǔ.
Jǔ had no great officers;
why is this recorded?
To criticize.
What is criticized here?
A great officer crossing the border to meet a bride
was contrary to ritual.
The Earl of Qǐ came to court.
The duke met with the Marquis of Qí at Chéngpú.
In the 28th year, in spring, the king's third month, on Jiǎyín day,
the men of Qí attacked Wèi.
The men of Wèi and the men of Qí fought,
and the men of Wèi were severely defeated.
Attacks are not dated,
why is this one dated?
Because they attacked on the very day they arrived.
When a battle is mentioned, an attack is not separately stated,
why does this text mention the attack?
Because they attacked on the very day they arrived.
In the Spring and Autumn Annals, the attackers are considered the guests,
and the attacked are considered the hosts,
therefore, Wèi is made the host in this record.
Why was Wèi made the host?
Because Wèi was without fault.
The defeated are usually referred to by their army,
why is Wèi not referred to by its army?
Because they had not yet properly formed their army.
In summer, the fourth month, on Dīngwèi day,
Zhūlóu's ruler, Suǒ, died.
In autumn,
Jīng attacked Zhèng.
The duke met with the men of Qí, Sòng, and Zhūlóu to rescue Zhèng.
In winter,
the wall of Wēi was built.
There was a great failure of the wheat and millet harvest.
Since the failure of the wheat and millet was observed in winter,
why does the text first mention building the wall of Wēi and then mention the crop failure?
To conceal the fact that a city was built in a famine year.
Zāng Sūn Chén requested grain from Qí.
What is meant by "requesting grain"?
It means he asked to buy grain.
Why is he not said to have been sent?
It is considered Zāng Sūn Chén's private undertaking.
Why was it considered his private undertaking?
When a gentleman governs a state,
he must have three years' supply stored up.
If there is one year of crop failure,
and he has to request grain,
it is recorded to criticize him.
In the 29th year, in spring,
the New Extended Stables were built.
What were the New Extended Stables?
They were a renovation of the old ones.
Renovations are not usually recorded,
why is this one recorded?
To criticize.
What is criticized here?
That in a famine year, there should be no renovations.
In summer,
the men of Zhèng invaded Xǔ.
In autumn,
there were fěi insects.
Why is this recorded?
To record an anomaly.
In winter, in the twelfth month,
Jì's Shū Jī died.
The walls of Zhū and Fáng were built.
In the 30th year, in spring, the king's first month.
In summer,
the army was stationed at Chéng.
In autumn, the seventh month,
the men of Qí subdued Zhāng.
What was Zhāng?
It was a remaining town of Jì.
What does "subdued" mean?
It means they took it.
If they took it, why not say "took it"?
To conceal for Duke Huán.
The taking of towns outside is not recorded,
why is this recorded?
Because it was completely annexed.
In the eighth month, on Guǐhài day,
Jì's Shū Jī was buried.
The burial of external wives is not recorded,
why is this recorded?
To express pity.
Why pity?
Her state had perished,
and she was buried only with the title Shū.
In the ninth month, on the first day Gēngwǔ,
there was a solar eclipse.
Drums were beaten and sacrificial animals used at the altar of the soil.
In winter,
the duke and the marquis of Qí met at Lǔ Jǐ.
The men of Qí attacked the Shān Róng.
This was the marquis of Qí,
why is he referred to as "men"?
To贬.
Why贬?
Master Simǎ said:
"Probably because his actions were too harsh."
This was likely a battle,
why is it not called a battle?
In the Spring and Autumn Annals, combat between equals is called a battle,
but between Duke Huán and the Róng Dí,
it was merely driving them away.
In the 31st year, in spring,
a terrace was built at Láng.
Why is this recorded?
To criticize.
What is criticized?
It overlooked the place where the people washed and rinsed.
In summer, the fourth month,
the earl of Xuē died.
A terrace was built at Xuē.
Why is this recorded?
To criticize.
What is criticized?
It was too far away.
In the sixth month,
the marquis of Qí came to present spoils from the Róng.
Qí was a great state,
why did its ruler personally come to present Róng spoils?
To intimidate us.
How did he intimidate us?
He displayed his captured banners as he passed through our state.
In autumn,
a terrace was built at Qín.
Why is this recorded?
To criticize.
What is criticized?
It overlooked the capital.
In winter,
there was no rain.
Why is this recorded?
To record an anomaly.
In the 32nd year, in spring,
the wall of Xiǎogǔ was built.
In summer,
the duke of Sòng and the marquis of Qí met at Liángqiū.
In autumn, the seventh month, on Guǐsì day,
the nobleman Yá died.
Why is he not referred to as "younger brother"?
Because he was executed.
If he was executed, why not say he was assassinated?
To conceal for Jìzǐ the fact that he killed him.
Why conceal for Jìzǐ the killing?
Because Jìzǐ's suppression of evil
was not treated as a state judicial case;
it was in accordance with Jìzǐ's heart that it was concealed for him.
How did Jìzǐ suppress the evil?
Duke Zhuāng was ill,
and about to die.
He summoned Jìzǐ due to his illness.
When Jìzǐ arrived, he entrusted him with the governance of the state,
saying:
"If I do not recover from this illness,
to whom shall I hand over the state of Lǔ?"
Jìzǐ said:
"Bān is alive; why should my lord worry?"
The duke said:
"How could it be so straightforward?
Yá said to me:
'In Lǔ, succession alternates between son and brother,
and you, my lord, already know this.
Qìngfù is alive.'"
Jìzǐ said:
"How dare he?
Is he planning to rebel?
How dare he?"
Soon, Yá's plot to assassinate was fully prepared.
Jìzǐ mixed poison and made him drink it,
saying:
"If you, nobleman, follow my words and drink this,
then surely you can avoid being executed and ridiculed by all under heaven,
and will surely have descendants in Lǔ.
If you do not follow my words and refuse to drink this,
then you will surely be executed and ridiculed by all under heaven,
and will have no descendants in Lǔ."
Thereupon, he followed his words and drank it.
He drank it at the place of Wúlěi shì,
and died when he reached Wáng dī.
The nobleman Yá was then about to act.
Why is the wording the same as for one who personally assassinated?
For the ruler and kin, one should not have intentions (to harm);
if one has such intentions, he is to be executed.
Then, was this considered good?
It is said: Yes.
When killing the crown prince or maternal brothers, directly referring to the ruler
is to emphasize the gravity.
Jìzǐ killed his maternal elder brother;
why is this considered good?
In carrying out execution, one cannot avoid acting against an elder brother;
such is the duty between ruler and minister.
Then why did he not execute him directly?
But poisoned him instead?
To carry out execution against an elder brother,
and to conceal it and evade direct action,
making it appear as if he died of illness,
is the way of cherishing one's kin.
In the eighth month, on Guǐhài day,
the duke died in the Lù qǐn.
What is the Lù qǐn?
It is the main resting chamber.
In winter, the tenth month, on Yǐwèi day,
Zǐ Bān died.
When a son dies, it is recorded as "son died";
why here is it recorded as "Zǐ Bān died"?
While the ruler is alive, he is called the crown prince.
After the ruler's death, he is called "Zǐ [name]."
After burial, he is called "Zǐ,"
and after the passing of the year, he is called "Duke."
When Zǐ Bān died,
why was his burial not recorded?
Because he was a ruler who had not passed the year (of succession).
If he had a son, a temple would be established;
if a temple is established, the burial is recorded.
If he had no son, no temple is established;
if no temple is established, the burial is not recorded.
The nobleman Qìngfù went to Qí.
The Dí attacked Xíng.
First year, spring, the king's first month.
Why does it not say the duke ascended the throne?
When succeeding a murdered ruler, it is not said that he ascended the throne.
Who did he succeed?
He succeeded Zǐ Bān.
Who murdered Zǐ Bān?
It was Qìngfù.
When killing the nobleman Yá,
who was then about to act,
Jìzǐ could not avoid (taking action).
Qìngfù murdered the ruler;
why was he not executed?
Though he had intentions, he could not be prevented;
(this was) suppressing evil.
Afterward, it was too late to catch him,
and as the criminal case was attributed to someone,
without probing the actual circumstances to execute him,
was the way of cherishing one's kin.
To whom was the criminal case attributed?
It was attributed to the servant Dèng Hù Yuè.
Why was the criminal case attributed to the servant Dèng Hù Yuè?
While Duke Zhuāng was alive,
Yuè had once been licentious in the palace,
and Zǐ Bān seized and whipped him.
After Duke Zhuāng died,
Qìngfù said to Yuè:
"The humiliation Bān inflicted on you,
no one in the state is unaware of;
why not assassinate him?"
He made him assassinate Zǐ Bān,
then executed Dèng Hù Yuè and attributed the crime to him.
When Jìzǐ arrived, he did not change this.
The men of Qí rescued Xíng.
Summer, the sixth month, on Xīnyǒu day,
we buried our ruler Duke Zhuāng.
Autumn, the eighth month,
the duke and the marquis of Qí made a covenant at Luògū.
Jìzǐ came back.
Why is he referred to as Jìzǐ?
Because he was worthy.
What does "came back" mean?
It expresses joy at his return.
Winter,
Qí Zhòngsūn came.
Who is Qí Zhòngsūn?
It is the nobleman Qìngfù.
If he is the nobleman Qìngfù, why is he called Qí Zhòngsūn?
He is associated with Qí.
Why associate him with Qí?
To treat him as an outsider.
Why treat him as an outsider?
The Spring and Autumn Annals conceal for the honored,
for the kin,
and for the worthy.
Zǐ Nǚzǐ said:
"Taking the Spring and Autumn Annals as the Spring and Autumn Annals,
there is no Zhòngsūn in Qí;
could it be our Zhòngsūn?"
Second year, spring, the king's first month,
the men of Qí moved Yáng.
Summer, the fifth month, on Yǐyǒu day,
the jì sacrifice was held for Duke Zhuāng.
Why does it say "jì"?
Saying "jì"
means it was not yet permissible to hold the jì sacrifice.
Why was it not yet permissible?
Because the three-year mourning period was not over.
It had been three years;
why say it was not three years?
The three-year mourning period
actually consists of twenty-five months.
Why does it say "for Duke Zhuāng"?
Because it was not yet permissible to refer to the temple.
Why was it not yet permissible to refer to the temple?
Because it was still within the three-year period.
Why was the jì sacrifice for Duke Zhuāng recorded?
To criticize.
What is criticized here?
Criticizing the beginning of not observing the three-year mourning.
Autumn, the eighth month, on Xīnchǒu day,
the duke died.
Why is the place of the duke's death not recorded?
To conceal it.
What is concealed?
That he was murdered.
Who murdered him?
It was Qìngfù.
When killing the nobleman Yá,
who was then about to act,
Jìzǐ could not avoid (taking action).
Qìngfù murdered two rulers; why was he not executed?
Having intentions and being unavoidable was to suppress evil.
Afterward, it was too late to catch him;
pursuing slowly and letting the criminal escape
is the way of cherishing one's kin.
In the ninth month,
Lady Jiāng shì fled to Zhūlóu.
In winter,
Gāo Zǐ of Qí came to form a covenant.
Who was Gāo Zǐ?
He was a senior official of Qí.
Why is he not referred to as an envoy?
Because we had no ruler.
Then why is his personal name not mentioned?
Out of joy for him.
Why joy regarding him?
Because he rectified us.
How did he rectify us?
Duke Zhuāng died,
Zǐ Bān was assassinated,
Duke Mǐn was assassinated,
with three rulers dead in succession,
the state was left without a ruler for a full year.
Had Qí taken over Lǔ,
it would not have needed to raise an army,
but could have done so by mere words.
Duke Huán sent Gāo Zǐ leading the troops of Nányáng,
established Duke Xī and fortified Lǔ.
Some say the fortification extended from Lùmén to Zhēngmén,
others say from Zhēngmén to Lìmén.
The people of Lǔ to this day consider it a praiseworthy story,
saying:
"We still look hopefully to Gāo Zǐ."
In the twelfth month,
the Dí invaded Wèi.
Zhèng abandoned its army.
What is meant by 'Zhèng abandoned its army'?
It detested its commander.
The Earl of Zhèng detested Gāo Kè,
sent him to command the army,
then expelled him and would not take him back -
this is the way to abandon an army.
First year, spring, the king's first month.
Why does the text not say the duke ascended the throne?
Because he succeeded a murdered ruler.
A son does not speak of ascending the throne.
This was not a son,
so why is he called 'son'?
Because ministers and sons follow the same rule.
The armies of Qí, Sòng, and Cáo encamped at Nièběi,
to rescue Xíng.
When rescuing, one does not mention encamping,
so why does this mention encamping?
Because they did not reach the matter in time.
What does 'not reaching in time' mean?
Xíng had already perished.
Who caused its demise?
It was the Dí who destroyed it.
Why does it not say the Dí destroyed it?
To conceal for Duke Huán.
Why conceal for Duke Huán?
Above, there was no Son of Heaven;
below, there were no regional chiefs.
When among the feudal lords under heaven there were those who destroyed each other,
if Duke Huán could not rescue them,
then Duke Huán was shamed by it.
Why mention encamping first and rescuing afterwards?
Because it was the ruler's action.
If it was the ruler's action, why call it 'armies'?
Because it does not agree with the feudal lords arbitrarily installing.
Why not agree?
In substance, it agrees,
but in wording, it does not.
Why does the wording not agree?
Because according to the principle for feudal lords, they should not arbitrarily install.
If feudal lords should not arbitrarily install,
then why say that in substance it agrees?
Because above, there was no Son of Heaven;
below, there were no regional chiefs.
When among the feudal lords under heaven there were those who destroyed each other,
if one had the power to rescue them,
then rescuing them was permissible.
In summer, the sixth month,
Xíng moved to Chényí.
What does 'moved' mean?
It was their own intention.
What does 'was moved' mean?
It was not their intention.
The armies of Qí, Sòng, and Cáo walled Xíng.
This is the same event,
so why repeat 'the armies of Qí, Sòng, and Cáo'?
If the armies were not mentioned again,
there would be no way to know it was the same event.
In autumn, the seventh month, on Wùchén,
Lady Jiāng Shì died in Yí,
and the people of Qí brought her back.
What was Yí?
It was Qí territory.
If it was Qí territory, why say 'the people of Qí brought her back'?
The lady died in Yí,
so the people of Qí brought her back.
The lady died in Yí,
so why did the people of Qí bring her back?
Duke Huán had summoned her and strangled her.
The people of Chǔ attacked Zhèng.
In the eighth month,
the duke met with the Marquis of Qí, the Duke of Sòng, the Earl of Zhèng, the Earl of Cáo, and a person from Zhūlóu at Chēng.
In the ninth month,
the duke defeated the army of Zhūlóu at Yīng.
In winter, the tenth month, on Rénwǔ,
Gōngzǐ Yǒu led troops and defeated the army of Jǔ at Lí,
capturing Jǔ Rú.
Who was Jǔ Rú?
He was a senior official of Jǔ.
Jǔ had no senior officials,
so why is this recorded?
To magnify Jìzǐ's capture.
Why magnify Jìzǐ's capture?
Jìzǐ dealt with internal troubles with rectitude,
and resisted external troubles with rectitude.
How did he resist external troubles with rectitude?
Gōngzǐ Qìngfù assassinated Duke Mǐn,
fled and went to Jǔ,
the people of Jǔ expelled him,
he was about to pass through Qí,
but the people of Qí would not receive him,
so he turned back and lodged on the banks of the Wèn River,
sending Gōngzǐ Xīsī to enter and request.
Jìzǐ said:
"The gōngzǐ cannot enter;
if he enters, he will be killed."
Xīsī could not bear to report back to Qìngfù,
so from the southern bank,
he faced north and wept.
Qìngfù heard it and said:
"Alas!
This is Xīsī's voice;
it is over."
He said:
"I cannot enter."
Thereupon, he lifted the carriage pole and hanged himself.
The people of Jǔ heard of it and said:
"We have obtained your criminal,
and will seek ransom from Lǔ."
The people of Lǔ did not give it,
so for this reason, they raised an army and attacked Lǔ.
Jìzǐ awaited them and engaged in a formal battle.
In the twelfth month, on Dīngsì,
the funeral of the lady of the clan arrived from Qí.
Why is the lady not referred to as Jiāng Shì?
To condemn her.
Why condemn her?
Because she was involved in assassinating the duke.
Then why was she not condemned at the time of the assassination?
Condemnation must occur at the most significant moment,
and nothing was more significant than her return with the funeral.
In the second year, in spring, the king's first month,
the city of Chǔqiū was fortified.
Who fortified it?
It was fortifying Wèi.
Why is it not stated that Wèi was fortified?
Because it had been destroyed.
Who destroyed it?
It was probably the Dí who destroyed it.
Why is it not stated that the Dí destroyed it?
To conceal for Duke Huán.
Why conceal for Duke Huán?
Above, there was no Son of Heaven;
below, there were no regional chiefs.
When among the feudal lords under heaven there were those who destroyed and perished each other,
if Duke Huán could not save them,
then Duke Huán would be ashamed of it.
Then who fortified it?
Duke Huán fortified it.
Why is it not stated that Duke Huán fortified it?
Because it does not approve of feudal lords arbitrarily enfeoffing.
Why not approve?
In substance, it is approved, but in wording, it is not.
Why in wording is it not approved?
The principle for feudal lords is that they may not arbitrarily enfeoff.
The principle for feudal lords is that they may not arbitrarily enfeoff,
then what does it mean that in substance it is approved?
Above, there was no Son of Heaven;
below, there were no regional chiefs.
When among the feudal lords under heaven there were those who destroyed and perished each other,
if one had the power to save them,
then saving them was permissible.
In summer, in the fifth month, on the xīnsì day,
we buried our lesser lord, Lady Āi Jiāng.
Who was Lady Āi Jiāng?
She was the wife of Duke Zhuāng.
The armies of Yú and Jìn destroyed Xiàyáng.
Yú was a small state;
why is it placed above the great state?
To make Yú the chief culprit.
Why make Yú the chief culprit?
Yú accepted bribes,
lent the path to the state-destroyers,
and thereby brought about its own demise.
How did it accept bribes?
Duke Xiàn summoned his ministers and asked them,
saying:
"I, the solitary one, lie down at night but cannot sleep;
what is the reason for this?"
Among the ministers, one came forward to reply,
saying:
"Is it that you sleep restlessly?
Or are there some attendants not by your side?"
Duke Xiàn did not respond.
Xún Xì came forward and said:
"Is it about Yú and Guō?"
Duke Xiàn bowed and invited him forward,
then entered with him to strategize, saying:
"I wish to attack Guō,
but Yú would rescue it;
attack Yú, and Guō would rescue it.
What should be done?
I wish to discuss it with you."
Xún Xì replied:
"If my lord uses your servant's plan,
then today we take Guō,
and tomorrow we take Yú;
what is my lord worried about?"
Duke Xiàn said:
"Then how to proceed?"
Xún Xì said:
"Request to take the steeds from Qūchǎn,
and the white jade from Chuíjí to send there;
it will surely be obtainable.
As for the treasures—take them from the inner treasury,
store them in the outer treasury;
the horses—take them from the inner stable,
tie them in the outer stable;
what would my lord lose?"
Duke Xiàn said:
"Agreed.
Even so,
Gōng Zhī Qí is still there;
what about that?"
Xún Xì said:
"Gōng Zhī Qí is wise, indeed he is wise.
Even so,
the Duke of Yú is greedy and fond of treasures;
upon seeing the treasures,
he will certainly not follow his words.
I request to proceed with sending them."
Thereupon, they proceeded to send them.
The Duke of Yú saw the treasures,
and gave his consent.
Gōng Zhī Qí indeed remonstrated:
"The 'Record' says:
'If the lips are gone, the teeth will be cold.'
Yú and Guō rescue each other,
not as a favor to one another;
for if Jìn takes Guō today,
then tomorrow Yú will follow and perish.
I beg my lord not to consent."
The Duke of Yú did not follow his words,
and ultimately lent the path to take Guō.
Returning after four years,
they turned around and took Yú.
The Duke of Yú came, holding the treasures and leading the horses.
Xún Xì saw him and said:
"How was your servant's plan?"
Duke Xiàn said:
"Your plan has already been carried out;
the treasures are still my treasures.
Even so,
the teeth of my horses have also grown longer."
This was probably teasing him.
What was Xiàyáng?
It was a city of Guō.
Why is it not attached to Guō?
Because it was treated as a state.
Why treat it as a state?
Because the ruler was present there.
In autumn, in the ninth month,
the Hóu of Qí, the Gōng of Sòng, the men of Jiāng, and the men of Huáng made a covenant at Guànzé.
Who were the men of Jiāng and the men of Huáng?
It is the term for distant states.
The distant states arrived;
then why does the central states only mention Qí and Sòng arriving?
The great states are mentioned as Qí and Sòng,
the distant states as Jiāng and Huáng,
then because the rest were considered as none daring not to arrive.
In winter, in the tenth month,
there was no rain.
Why is this recorded?
To record an anomaly.
The men of Chǔ invaded Zhèng.
In the third year, in spring, the king's first month,
there was no rain.
In summer, in the fourth month,
there was no rain.
Why is this recorded?
To record an anomaly.
The men of Xú took Shū.
Why does it say they took it?
Because it was easy.
In the sixth month,
it rained.
Why does it say it rained in the sixth month?
Because previously it rained but not heavily.
In autumn,
the Hóu of Qí, the Gōng of Sòng, the men of Jiāng, and the men of Huáng met at Yánggǔ.
This was a great meeting;
why is it mentioned at the end?
Duke Huán said:
"Do not block valleys,
do not hoard grain,
do not change the appointed heir,
do not make a concubine the wife."
In winter,
Gōngzǐ Yǒu went to Qí to attend a covenant.
What does 'attend a covenant' mean?
It means going to make a covenant there.
What does it mean when it says 'came to covenant'?
It means coming to make a covenant with us.
The men of Chǔ attacked Zhèng.
In the fourth year, in spring, the king's first month,
the Duke met with the Hóu of Qí, the Gōng of Sòng, the Hóu of Chén, the Hóu of Wèi, the Bó of Zhèng, the Nán of Xǔ, and the Bó of Cáo to invade Cài.
Cài collapsed.
What does 'collapse' mean?
It means those below rebelled against those above.
For a state, it is called collapse;
for a city, it is called rebellion.
Thereupon, they attacked Chǔ,
and encamped at Xíng.
Why does it say they encamped at Xíng?
Because there was waiting.
Waiting for whom?
Waiting for Qū Wán.
In summer,
the ruler of Xǔ, Xīnchén, passed away.
Chǔ's Qū Wán came to form a covenant with the army,
and they covenanted at Shàolíng.
Who was Qū Wán?
He was a senior official of Chǔ.
Why is he not referred to as an envoy?
To honor Qū Wán.
Why honor Qū Wán?
Because he stood up to Duke Huán.
Why mention covenanting with the army and covenanting at Shàolíng?
Because the army was at Shàolíng.
If the army was at Shàolíng,
then why mention the covenant twice?
To express joy at Chǔ's submission.
What does it mean to express joy at Chǔ's submission?
When there is a true king, Chǔ is the last to submit;
when there is no true king, Chǔ is the first to rebel.
They are barbarians,
who repeatedly harass the Central States,
with southern and northern barbarians interacting.
The Central States hang by a thread,
but Duke Huán saved the Central States and repelled the barbarians,
finally pacifying Jīng,
which is the work of a true king.
Why use the word "came"?
To acknowledge Duke Huán as the leader.
There were events before this,
and there will be events after,
so why single out this occasion?
To acknowledge Duke Huán as the leader?
To record his achievements in order.
The men of Qí seized Chén's Yuán Táotú.
What was Táotú's crime?
He diverted the army's route.
How did he divert the army's route?
Táotú said to Duke Huán:
"Since you have subdued the southern barbarians,
why not turn the army to follow the coast eastward,
subdue the eastern barbarians, and then return?"
Duke Huán said:
"Agreed."
Thereupon, he turned the army to follow the coast eastward,
and they became deeply mired in the marshlands.
He then looked back and seized Táotú.
Why are some who seize others called by their feudal title,
and others called "men"?
Those called by their feudal title when seizing
are carrying out a hegemon's punishment.
Those called "men" when seizing
are not carrying out a hegemon's punishment.
Here, a guilty person was seized,
so why is it not considered a hegemon's punishment?
In ancient times, when the Duke of Zhōu campaigned east, the western states complained;
when he campaigned west, the eastern states complained.
Duke Huán borrowed a route through Chén to attack Chǔ,
so the people of Chén did not want his return route to pass through their land,
because the army's conduct was improper.
Not rectifying his army's conduct but seizing Táotú—
the punishments of the ancients
were not like this.
In autumn,
they, along with the men of Jiāng and Huáng, attacked Chén.
In the eighth month,
the duke arrived from attacking Chǔ.
Chǔ had already submitted,
so why record the arrival from the attack?
Because Chǔ broke the covenant.
The funeral of Duke Mù of Xǔ was held.
In winter, in the twelfth month,
Gōngsūn Cí led troops to join the men of Qí, Sòng, Wèi, Zhèng, Xǔ, and Cáo in invading Chén.
In the fifth year, spring,
the Hóu of Jìn killed his heir apparent Shēnshēng.
Why is it directly stated that the Hóu of Jìn killed him?
Killing an heir apparent or maternal brother and directly naming the ruler
is to emphasize the gravity of the act.
Qí's Bó Jī came,
to present her son in court.
What does it mean that she came to present her son in court?
It is an internal expression,
meaning she came to court together with her son.
In summer,
Gōngsūn Cí went to Móu.
The duke, along with the Hóu of Qí, Gōng of Sòng, Hóu of Chén, Hóu of Wèi, Bó of Zhèng, ruler of Xǔ, and Bó of Cáo, met with the king's heir apparent at Shǒudài.
Why single out the meeting with the king's heir apparent?
Because the heir apparent is noble,
the heir apparent is like the heir of generations.
In autumn, the eighth month,
the feudal lords covenanted at Shǒudài.
Why are the feudal lords not listed in order?
For matters that appear twice,
the first lists them in detail, the second generally.
The Bó of Zhèng fled back without joining the covenant.
What does it mean that he fled back without joining the covenant?
He could not be made to covenant.
If he could not be made to covenant,
then why say he fled back?
Lǔzǐ said:
"Probably to avoid having the few offend the many."
The men of Chǔ destroyed Xián,
and the ruler of Xián fled to Huáng.
On the first day of the ninth month, wùshēn,
there was a solar eclipse.
In winter,
the men of Jìn seized the Gōng of Yú.
Yú had already been destroyed,
so why say he was seized?
To not acknowledge the destruction.
Why not acknowledge the destruction?
"Destroy" is a favorable term for a perishing state.
"Destroy" implies that both high and low exerted their strength together.
In the sixth year, spring, the royal first month.
In summer,
the duke joined the Hóu of Qí, Gōng of Sòng, Hóu of Chén, Hóu of Wèi, and Bó of Cáo in attacking Zhèng,
surrounding Xīnchéng.
Normally, a city is not said to be surrounded,
so why mention surrounding here?
Because it was a stronghold.
In autumn,
the men of Chǔ surrounded Xǔ,
and the feudal lords then rescued Xǔ.
In winter,
the duke arrived from attacking Zhèng.
In the seventh year, spring,
the men of Qí attacked Zhèng.
In summer,
the ruler of Xiǎozhūlóu came to court.
Zhèng killed its senior official Shēn Hóu.
Why is it said the state killed him?
Saying the state killed him
is the expression for when a ruler kills a senior official.
In autumn, the seventh month,
the duke joined the Hóu of Qí, Gōng of Sòng, heir apparent Kuǎn of Chén, and heir apparent Huá of Zhèng,
in covenanting at Níngmǔ.
The Bó of Cáo, Bān, passed away.
Gōngzǐ Yǒu went to Qí.
In winter,
the funeral of Duke Zhāo of Cáo was held.
In the eighth year, spring, the royal first month,
the duke joined the king's man, Hóu of Qí, Gōng of Sòng, Hóu of Wèi, ruler of Xǔ, Bó of Cáo, heir apparent Kuǎn of Chén, and heir apparent Huá of Zhèng,
in covenanting at Táo.
Who was the king's man?
A minor official.
Why is he listed above the feudal lords?
Because of the former king's command.
The Bó of Zhèng begged to join the covenant.
What does "begged to join the covenant" mean?
He requested to join from his own place.
How did he request to join from his own place?
Probably by offering a toast.
In summer,
the Dí attacked Jìn.
In autumn, in the seventh month,
a di sacrifice was held in the Grand Temple,
and the Lady was brought to it.
What does "used" mean?
"Used" means it was inappropriate to use.
What does "brought" mean?
"Brought" means it was inappropriate to bring her.
Holding the di sacrifice and bringing the Lady
was contrary to ritual.
Why is the Lady not referred to as of the Jiāng clan?
To贬 (denounce).
Why denounce?
To criticize making a concubine the wife.
How was a concubine made the wife?
It was under pressure from the Qí escort maiden who arrived first.
In winter, on the dīngwèi day of the twelfth month,
the Heavenly King passed away.
In the ninth year, in spring, the king's third month, on the dīngchǒu day,
the Duke of Sòng, Yù Yuē, died.
Why was his burial not recorded?
To conceal for Duke Xiāng.
In summer,
the Duke met with Minister Zhōu Gōng, the Marquis of Qí, the Viscount of Sòng, the Marquis of Wèi, the Earl of Zhèng, the Baron of Xǔ, and the Earl of Cáo at Kuíqiū.
Who is Minister Zhōu Gōng?
He is one who administers governance for the Son of Heaven.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the yǐyǒu day,
Bó Jī died.
Why is her death recorded when she had not yet married?
She was betrothed.
When a woman is betrothed,
she is given a courtesy name and receives a hairpin,
and if she dies, she is mourned with the funeral rites of an adult.
In the ninth month, on the wùchén day,
the feudal lords made a covenant at Kuíqiū.
The covenants of Duke Huán were not dated;
why is this one dated?
To express danger.
What danger?
At the meeting at Guànzé,
Duke Huán had a heart concerned for the Central States,
and those who came without being summoned were the people of Jiāng and Huáng.
At the meeting at Kuíqiū,
Duke Huán was shaken and arrogant,
and nine states rebelled.
What does "shaken" mean?
It means he was agitated.
What does "arrogant" mean?
It means he thought no one was like him.
On the jiǎxū day,
the Marquis of Jìn, Guǐ Zhū, died.
In winter,
Lǐ Kè of Jìn assassinated his ruler's son Xī Qí.
This was a ruler who had not passed the year of mourning;
why say "assassinated his ruler's son Xī Qí"?
It is the designation for assassinating a ruler who has not passed the year of mourning.
In the tenth year, in spring, the king's first month,
the Duke went to Qí.
The Dí destroyed Wēn.
The Viscount of Wēn fled to Wèi.
Lǐ Kè of Jìn assassinated his ruler Zhuó Zǐ and his great officer Xún Xī.
What does "and" mean?
It means implicated.
There have been many assassinations of rulers;
are there none implicated besides this?
It is said:
"There were Kǒng Fù and Qiú Mù, both were implicated."
Besides Kǒng Fù and Qiú Mù,
are there none implicated?
It is said:
"There are."
If there are, why is this recorded?
Because of worthiness.
Why is Xún Xī considered worthy?
Xún Xī can be said to have not gone back on his word.
How did he not go back on his word?
Xī Qí and Zhuó Zǐ
were the sons of Lí Jī,
and Xún Xī was their tutor.
Lí Jī was a beauty of the state.
Duke Xiàn loved her deeply,
wished to establish her son,
and thus killed the heir Shēn Shēng.
Shēn Shēng
was tutored by Lǐ Kè.
Duke Xiàn fell ill,
and when near death,
said to Xún Xī:
"What must a scholar do to be called trustworthy?"
Xún Xī replied:
"If the dead could return to life,
and the living feel no shame before their words,
then they can be called trustworthy."
Duke Xiàn died,
and Xī Qí was established.
Lǐ Kè said to Xún Xī:
"The ruler killed the rightful and established the unrightful,
discarded the elder and established the younger;
what is to be done?
I wish to discuss it with you."
Xún Xī said:
"The ruler once questioned me,
and I replied:
'If the dead could return to life,
and the living feel no shame before their words,
then they can be called trustworthy.'"
Lǐ Kè knew he could not be persuaded,
withdrew, and assassinated Xī Qí.
Xún Xī established Zhuó Zǐ,
Lǐ Kè assassinated Zhuó Zǐ,
and Xún Xī died for it.
Xún Xī can be said to have not gone back on his word.
In summer,
the Marquis of Qí and the Baron of Xǔ attacked the Northern Róng.
Jìn killed its great officer Lǐ Kè.
Lǐ Kè assassinated two rulers;
then why not use the language of punishing a villain?
He was a great officer of Duke Huì.
Then who established Duke Huì?
Lǐ Kè did.
Lǐ Kè assassinated Xī Qí and Zhuó Zǐ,
and welcomed Duke Huì in.
Lǐ Kè established Duke Huì;
then why did Duke Huì kill him?
Duke Huì said:
"You have already killed those two youths;
you will next plot against me.
Being your ruler,
is it not perilous?"
Thereupon he killed him.
Then why not mention Duke Huì's entry?
Jìn's not mentioning entry or exit is to conceal for Duke Wén.
When Qí's Xiǎo Bái entered Qí,
why not conceal for Duke Huán?
Duke Huán's reign was long,
and his goodness was evident to the world,
so his original faults were not concealed.
Duke Wén's reign was short,
and his goodness was not yet evident to the world,
so his original faults were concealed.
In autumn, in the seventh month.
In winter,
there was heavy hail.
Why is this recorded?
To record an anomaly.
In the eleventh year, in spring,
Jìn killed its great officer Pī Zhèngfù.
In summer,
the Duke and his wife, Lady Jiāng, met with the Marquis of Qí at Yánggǔ.
In autumn, in the eighth month,
a great rain sacrifice was held.
In winter,
the people of Chǔ attacked Huáng.
In the twelfth year, in spring, the king's third month, on the gēngwǔ day,
there was a solar eclipse.
In summer,
the people of Chǔ destroyed Huáng.
In autumn, in the seventh month.
In winter, in the twelfth month, on the dīngchǒu day,
the Marquis of Chén, Chǔ Jiù, died.
In the thirteenth year, in spring,
the Dí invaded Wèi.
In summer, the fourth month,
Duke Xuān of Chén was buried.
The Duke met with the Marquis of Qí, Duke of Sòng, Marquis of Chén, Marquis of Wèi, Earl of Zhèng, Baron of Xǔ, and Earl of Cáo at Xián.
In autumn, the ninth month,
a great rain sacrifice was held.
In winter,
Prince Yǒu went to Qí.
In the fourteenth year, in spring,
the feudal lords walled Yuánlíng.
Who walled it?
They walled it for Qǐ.
Why did they wall it for Qǐ?
Because it had been destroyed.
Who destroyed it?
It was probably coerced by Xú and Jǔ.
Why is it not stated that Xú and Jǔ coerced it?
To conceal for Duke Huán.
Why conceal for Duke Huán?
Above, there was no Son of Heaven;
below, there were no regional chiefs.
When among the feudal lords under heaven there were those who destroyed each other,
if Duke Huán could not save them,
then Duke Huán would be ashamed of it.
Then who walled it?
Duke Huán walled it.
Why is it not stated that Duke Huán walled it?
Because he did not agree with feudal lords arbitrarily enfiefing.
Why did he not agree?
In substance, he agreed, but in wording, he did not.
Why in wording did he not agree?
Because it was against the principle for feudal lords to arbitrarily enfief.
Since it was against the principle for feudal lords to arbitrarily enfief,
then why say that in substance he agreed?
Above, there was no Son of Heaven;
below, there were no regional chiefs.
When among the feudal lords under heaven there were those who destroyed each other,
if one had the power to save them,
then saving them was permissible.
In summer, the sixth month,
Jì Jī and the Viscount of Zēng met at Fáng,
and she sent the Viscount of Zēng to come for an audience.
Why was the Viscount of Zēng sent by Jì Jī to come for an audience?
It is an internal expression.
He was not sent to come for an audience,
but was sent to request her for himself.
In autumn, on the eighth month, day Xīnmǎo,
Shālù collapsed.
What is Shālù?
It is a town on the river.
This is a town;
why is its collapse mentioned?
Because it was a surprise attack on the town.
Why is the collapse of Shālù recorded?
To record an anomaly.
Anomalies outside are not recorded;
why is this recorded?
To record the anomaly for all under heaven.
The Dí invaded Zhèng.
In winter,
Marquis Xī of Cài died.
In the fifteenth year, in spring, the royal first month,
the Duke went to Qí.
The men of Chǔ attacked Xú.
In the third month,
the Duke met with the Marquis of Qí, Duke of Sòng, Marquis of Chén, Marquis of Wèi, Earl of Zhèng, Baron of Xǔ, and Earl of Cáo to covenant at Mǔqiū,
then proceeded to station at Kuāng.
Gōngsūn Áo led the army and the great officers of the feudal lords to rescue Xú.
In summer, the fifth month,
there was an eclipse of the sun.
In autumn, the seventh month,
the army of Qí and the army of Cáo attacked Lì.
In the eighth month,
there were locusts.
In the ninth month,
the Duke arrived from the meeting.
Meetings of Duke Huán are not recorded with "arrived";
why is this one recorded with "arrived"?
Because it was prolonged.
Jì Jī returned to Zēng.
On the last day of the month, Jǐmǎo,
Yí Bó's temple was struck.
What is "the last day of the month"?
It means dark.
What is meant by "struck"?
It means lightning struck Yí Bó's temple.
Who was Yí Bó?
He was a trusted retainer of the Jì family.
If he was a trusted retainer of the Jì family, then he was a minor figure;
why is he referred to as Yí Bó?
To honor him.
Why honor him?
Because Heaven warned him,
hence he was honored.
Why is this recorded?
To record an anomaly.
In winter,
the men of Sòng attacked Cáo.
The men of Chǔ defeated Xú at Lóulín.
In the eleventh month, on day Rénxū,
the Marquis of Jìn and the Earl of Qín fought at Hán,
and the Marquis of Jìn was captured.
This was a regular battle;
why is it not stated that the army was defeated?
When the ruler is captured, it is not stated that the army was defeated.
In the sixteenth year, in spring, the royal first month, on the first day, Wùshēn,
five stones fell in Sòng.
In this month,
six kingfishers flew backward past the capital of Sòng.
Why are "fell" mentioned first and then "stones"?
"Fell stones" records the sound;
hearing their thudding sound,
looking at them, they were stones,
examining them, there were five.
What is meant by "this month"?
It means just within this month.
Why is the day not recorded?
Because it was the last day of the month.
If it was the last day, why not state "last day"?
The *Spring and Autumn Annals* do not record the last day.
If there is an event on the first day, it is recorded;
even if there is an event on the last day, it is not recorded.
Why are "six" mentioned first and then "kingfishers"?
"Six kingfishers flying backward" records the sight;
looking at them, there were six,
examining them, they were kingfishers,
and upon careful observation, they were flying backward.
Why are the five stones and six kingfishers recorded?
To record anomalies.
Anomalies outside are not recorded;
why are these recorded?
To record anomalies for the descendants of the king.
In the third month, on day Rénshēn,
Prince Jì Yǒu died.
Why is he referred to as Jì Yǒu?
Because he was worthy.
In summer, the fourth month, on day Bǐngshēn,
Jì Jī of Zēng died.
In autumn, the seventh month, on day Jiǎzǐ,
Gōngsūn Cí died.
In winter, the twelfth month,
the Duke met with the Marquis of Qí, Duke of Sòng, Marquis of Chén, Marquis of Wèi, Earl of Zhèng, Baron of Xǔ, Marquis of Xíng, and Earl of Cáo at Huái.
In the seventeenth year, in spring,
men of Qí and Xú attacked Yīngshì.
In summer,
Xiàng was destroyed.
Who destroyed it?
Qí destroyed it.
Why is it not stated that Qí destroyed it?
To conceal for Duke Huán.
The *Spring and Autumn Annals* conceal for the worthy;
this was the destruction of another state;
what worthiness is there?
The gentleman hates evil by detesting its beginning,
and loves good by rejoicing in its end.
Duke Huán once had the merit of continuing severed lines and preserving perishing states,
hence the gentleman conceals for him.
In autumn,
Lady Jiāng met with the Marquis of Qí at Biàn.
In the ninth month,
the Duke arrived from the meeting.
In winter, on the Yǐhài day of the twelfth month,
the Marquis of Qí, Xiǎobái, died.
In the eighteenth year, in spring, the royal first month,
the Duke of Sòng joined the Earl of Cáo, a man of Wèi, and a man of Zhūlóu in attacking Qí.
In summer,
an army rescued Qí.
In the fifth month, on the Wùyín day,
the army of Sòng and the army of Qí battled at Yǎn,
and the army of Qí was defeated.
Battles are not mentioned when there is an attack,
so why is an attack mentioned here?
The Duke of Sòng participated in the attack but not in the battle,
hence the mention of the attack.
In the Spring and Autumn Annals, the attacker is the guest,
and the attacked is the host.
Why was Qí not made the host?
It was in support of Duke Xiāng's campaign against Qí.
Why support Duke Xiāng's campaign against Qí?
When Duke Huán died,
Shù Diāo and Yì Yá contended for power,
and he was not buried,
so for this reason, they attacked.
The Dí rescued Qí.
In autumn, on the Dīnghài day of the eighth month,
Duke Huán of Qí was buried.
In winter,
men of Xíng and the Dí attacked Wèi.
In the nineteenth year, in spring, the royal third month,
men of Sòng seized the Viscount of Téng, Yīngqí.
In summer, in the sixth month,
men of Sòng, Cáo, and Zhūlóu made a covenant south of Cáo.
The Viscount of Zēng attended the covenant at Zhūlóu.
Why say "attended the covenant"?
It was because he arrived after the covenant.
On the Jǐyǒu day,
men of Zhūlóu seized the Viscount of Zēng,
and used him.
How was he used?
He was used at the altar of the soil.
How was he used at the altar of the soil?
They struck his nose to draw blood for the altar.
In autumn,
men of Sòng besieged Cáo.
Men of Wèi attacked Xíng.
In winter,
the Duke joined men of Chén, Cài, Chǔ, and Zhèng in making a covenant at Qí.
Liáng perished.
There is no mention of attackers here;
why does it say Liáng perished?
It perished by itself.
How did it perish by itself?
It rotted from within like a fish.
In the twentieth year, in spring,
the south gate was newly built.
Why is this recorded?
To criticize.
Why criticize this?
Because gates should follow ancient norms.
In summer,
the Viscount of Gào came to court.
Who is the Viscount of Gào?
He is a lord who lost his land.
Why is he not named?
It is the language of fraternal relations.
In the fifth month, on the Yǐsì day,
the Western Palace suffered a disaster.
What is the Western Palace?
It is a minor residence.
If it is a minor residence, why call it the Western Palace?
If there is a Western Palace, then there is an Eastern Palace.
Lǔzǐ said:
"From the existence of the Western Palace,
we also know that the feudal lords have three palaces."
Why is the disaster at the Western Palace recorded?
To record the disaster.
Men of Zhèng entered Huá.
In autumn,
men of Qí and the Dí made a covenant at Xíng.
In winter,
men of Chǔ attacked Suí.
In the twenty-first year, in spring,
the Dí invaded Wèi.
Men of Sòng, Qí, and Chǔ made a covenant at Lùshàng.
In summer,
there was a great drought.
Why is this recorded?
To record the disaster.
In autumn,
the Duke of Sòng, the Viscount of Chǔ, the Marquis of Chén, the Marquis of Cài, the Earl of Zhèng, the Baron of Xǔ, and the Earl of Cáo met at Huò,
and the Duke of Sòng was seized to attack Sòng.
Who seized him?
The Viscount of Chǔ seized him.
Why not say the Viscount of Chǔ seized him?
To not acknowledge a barbarian seizing a central state.
In winter,
the Duke attacked Zhūlóu.
A man of Chǔ sent Yí Shēn to present spoils of war.
This was the Viscount of Chǔ;
why is he referred to as a man?
To贬.

The Duke of Sòng and the Viscount of Chǔ had agreed to meet in a carriage meeting.
Prince Mùyí advised, saying:
"Chǔ is a barbarian state,
strong but without righteousness;

He ultimately went to the carriage meeting,

The Duke of Sòng said to Prince Mùyí:

The men of Chǔ said to the men of Sòng:

The men of Sòng responded:

a noble man does not drum the advance against an unformed ranks."

"Sent him to"

"Sent to"

This refers to the Marquis of Jìn.

Duke Wén expelled the Marquis of Wèi and set up Shūwǔ,

Wèi Yuánxuǎn returned to Wèi from Jìn.

This one captured his ruler,

To attribute the blame to Yuán Xuǎn.

Yuán Xuǎn's service to his lord,

The marquis of Jìn seized the earl of Cáo,
and distributed the invaded lands he had taken among the feudal lords,

Because it had been a long time.
Prince Suì went to Jìn.

Why is Lǔ's border sacrifice not according to ritual?
The Son of Heaven sacrifices to Heaven,

The Son of Heaven has the affairs of the四方望 sacrifices,

They are the望 sacrifices.

Why sacrifice to Tài Shān, the Hé River, and the sea?
Mountains and rivers that can moisten a hundred lǐ,

Touching the stones and emerging,

The Hé River and the sea moisten a thousand lǐ.

To criticize not performing the border sacrifice but performing the望 sacrifices.
In autumn, the seventh month.

Xián Gāo was a merchant of Zhèng,

To贬.

the duke ascended the throne.

What is meant by "Sīchéng"?

If he had not been called king, how do we know he had ascended the throne?
From the fact that feudal lords ascend the throne after the passing of the mourning year,

From the fact that the Son of Heaven is called king only after three years,
we also know that feudal lords are referred to as 'zǐ' within their domains for three years.
After the mourning year, they are called 'gōng',

It is because, considering the hearts of the people and ministers,
there cannot be a single day without a ruler;
considering the principle of continuity from beginning to end,
there cannot be two rulers in one year,
and there cannot be a full year without a ruler.
Considering the heart of a filial son,
he cannot bear to assume the full role for three years.

To criticize.

It is said: No.

The king should not make requests.
It is said: This is the son.
He inherited King Wén's legacy,

King Wén's laws prohibited making requests,
