They had not yet besieged Qí.
If they had not besieged Qí, then why is it said they besieged Qí?
To humble Qí.
Why humble Qí?
Because it repeatedly launched campaigns.
Some say it was due to its arrogance,
placing its heir above the feudal lords.
They took land from Zhūlóu from the Huò River.
Why mention "from the Huò River"?
Because the Huò was made the boundary.
Why say the Huò was made the boundary?
The Huò had shifted.
Jìsūn Sù went to Jìn.
The burial of Duke Chéng of Cáo took place.
In summer,
Sūn Línfǔ of Wèi led troops to attack Qí.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on xīnmǎo,
the Hóu of Qí, Yuàn, died.
Shì Gài of Jìn led troops to invade Qí,
reached Gǔ,
heard of the death of the Hóu of Qí,
and then returned.
What does "returned" mean?
It is a commendatory expression.
What is commendable about this?
It praises his not attacking a state in mourning.
He had received orders from his ruler to attack Qí;
then why praise his not attacking the mourning state?
When a senior minister goes out with his ruler's orders,
advance or retreat lies with the senior minister.
In the eighth month, on bǐngchén,
Zhòngsūn Miè died.
Qí killed its senior minister Gāo Hòu.
Zhèng killed its senior minister the Gōngzǐ Xǐ.
In winter,
the burial of Duke Líng of Qí took place.
The western outer wall was fortified.
Shūsūn Bào met with Shì Gài of Jìn at Kē.
Wǔchéng was fortified.
In the twentieth year, in spring, the first month of the royal calendar, on xīnhài,
Zhòngsūn Sù met with the men of Jǔ,
and they formed an alliance at Xiàng.
In summer, in the sixth month, on gēngshēn,

the duke met with the Hóu of Jìn, the Hóu of Qí, the Gōng of Sòng, the Hóu of Wèi, the Bó of Zhèng, the Bó of Cáo, the Zǐ of Jǔ, the Zǐ of Zhūlóu, the Zǐ of Téng, the Bó of Xuē, the Bó of Qǐ, and the Zǐ of Xiǎozhūlóu,
and they formed an alliance at Chányuān.
In autumn,
the duke arrived from the meeting.
Zhòngsūn Sù led troops to attack Zhūlóu.
Cài killed its senior minister the Gōngzǐ Xiè.
The Gōngzǐ Lǚ of Cài fled to Chǔ.
The younger brother Guāng of the Hóu of Chén fled to Chǔ.
Shū Lǎo went to Qí.
In winter, in the tenth month, on bǐngchén, the first day of the month,
there was an eclipse of the sun.
Jìsūn Sù went to Sòng.
In the twenty-first year, in spring, the first month of the royal calendar,
the duke went to Jìn.
Shùqí of Zhūlóu came fleeing with Qī and Lǘqiū.
Who was Shùqí of Zhūlóu?
A senior minister of Zhūlóu.
Zhūlóu had no senior ministers;
why is this recorded?
Because the land was important.
In summer,
the duke arrived from Jìn.
In autumn,
Luán Yíng of Jìn fled to Chǔ.
In the ninth month, on gēngxū, the first day of the month,
there was an eclipse of the sun.
In winter, in the tenth month, on gēngchén, the first day of the month,
there was an eclipse of the sun.
The Bó of Cáo came for a court visit.
The duke met with the Hóu of Jìn, the Hóu of Qí, the Gōng of Sòng, the Hóu of Wèi, the Bó of Zhèng, the Bó of Cáo, the Zǐ of Jǔ, and the Zǐ of Zhūlóu at Shāngrén.
In the eleventh month, on gēngzǐ,
Confucius was born.
In the twenty-second year, in spring, the first month of the royal calendar,
the duke arrived from the meeting.
In summer, the fourth month.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on xīnyǒu,
Shū Lǎo died.
In winter,

the duke met with the Hóu of Jìn, the Hóu of Qí, the Gōng of Sòng, the Hóu of Wèi, the Bó of Zhèng, the Bó of Cáo, the Zǐ of Jǔ, the Zǐ of Zhūlóu, the Zǐ of Téng, the Bó of Xuē, the Bó of Qǐ, and the Zǐ of Xiǎozhūlóu at Shāsuí.
The duke arrived from the meeting.
Chǔ killed its senior minister the Gōngzǐ Zhuīshū.
In the twenty-third year, in spring, in the second month of the royal calendar, on guǐyǒu, the first day of the month,
there was an eclipse of the sun.
In the third month, on jǐsì,
the Bó of Qǐ, Gài, died.
In summer,
Bíwǒ of Zhūlóu came fleeing.
Who was Bíwǒ of Zhūlóu?
A senior minister of Zhūlóu.
Zhūlóu had no senior ministers;
why is this recorded?
Because it was recent, it was recorded.
The burial of Duke Xiào of Qǐ took place.
Chén killed its senior ministers Qìng Hǔ and Qìng Yín.
The younger brother Guāng of the Hóu of Chén returned from Chǔ to Chén.
Luán Yíng of Jìn re-entered Jìn,
entering Qūwò.
What was Qūwò?
A city of Jìn.
Why say he entered Jìn,
and entered Qūwò?
Luán Yíng was about to enter Jìn,
but the men of Jìn would not admit him,
so he entered via Qūwò.
In autumn,
the Hóu of Qí attacked Wèi,
and then attacked Jìn.
In the eighth month,
Shūsūn Bào led troops to rescue Jìn,
and halted at Yōngyú.
Why mention rescuing first and then halting?
To first communicate the ruler's command.
On jǐmǎo,
Zhòngsūn Sù died.
In winter, in the tenth month, on yǐhài,
Zāngsūn Hé fled to Zhūlóu.
The men of Jìn killed Luán Yíng.
Why not say they killed their senior minister?
Because he was not their senior minister.
The Hóu of Qí launched a surprise attack on Jǔ.
In the twenty-fourth year, in spring,
Shūsūn Bào went to Jìn.
Zhòngsūn Jié led troops to invade Qí.
In summer,
the Viscount of Chǔ attacked Wú.
In autumn, on the first day of the seventh month, Jiǎzǐ,
there was an eclipse of the sun,
which was total.
Cuī Zhù of Qí led troops to attack Jǔ.
There was a great flood.
On the first day of the eighth month, Guǐsì,
there was an eclipse of the sun.

The Duke met with the Marquis of Jìn, the Duke of Sòng, the Marquis of Wèi, the Earl of Zhèng, the Earl of Cáo, the Viscount of Jǔ, the Viscount of Zhūlóu, the Viscount of Téng, the Earl of Xuē, the Earl of Qǐ, and the Viscount of Xiǎo Zhūlóu at Chényí.
In winter,
the Viscount of Chǔ, the Marquis of Cài, the Marquis of Chén, and the Baron of Xǔ attacked Zhèng.
The Duke arrived from the meeting.
Chén Qián Yíjiù fled to Chǔ.
Shūsūn Bào went to the capital.
There was a great famine.
In the twenty-fifth year, in spring,
Cuī Zhù of Qí led troops to attack our northern borders.
In summer, in the fifth month, on Yǐhài,
Cuī Zhù of Qí assassinated his ruler, Guāng.

The Duke met with the Marquis of Jìn, the Duke of Sòng, the Marquis of Wèi, the Earl of Zhèng, the Earl of Cáo, the Viscount of Jǔ, the Viscount of Zhūlóu, the Viscount of Téng, the Earl of Xuē, the Earl of Qǐ, and the Viscount of Xiǎo Zhūlóu at Chényí.
In the sixth month, on Rénzǐ,
Gōngsūn Shězhī of Zhèng led troops and entered Chén.
In autumn, in the eighth month, on Jǐsì,
the feudal lords made a covenant together at Zhòngqiū.
The Duke arrived from the meeting.
The Marquis of Wèi entered Chényí.
What is Chényí?
It is a town of Wèi.
Why does it not say he entered Wèi?
To conceal that the ruler had been assassinated.
Qū Jiàn of Chǔ led troops and destroyed Shūjiū.
In winter,
Gōngsūn Cuó of Zhèng led troops to attack Chén.
In the twelfth month,
the Viscount of Wú, Yè, attacked Chǔ,
assaulted the gate of Cháo,
and died.
What does "assaulted the gate of Cháo and died" mean?
It means he died upon entering the gate of Cháo.
What does "died upon entering the gate of Cháo" mean?
It means he died after entering the gate of Cháo.
Why is the Viscount of Wú, Yè, referred to by his personal name?
Because he was wounded and turned back,
and died before reaching his quarters.
In the twenty-sixth year, in spring, in the royal second month, on Xīnmǎo,
Nìng Xǐ of Wèi assassinated his ruler, Piào.
Sūn Línfǔ of Wèi entered Qī and rebelled.
On Jiǎwǔ,
the Marquis of Wèi, Kàn, returned again to Wèi.
This conceals that the ruler had been assassinated.
Why does it say "returned again"?
To express disapproval of Piào.
Why disapprove of Piào?
There was no justification for Piào's establishment at that time.
Then why not mention Piào's establishment?
Not mentioning Piào's establishment
is to express disapproval of the Marquis of Wèi.
In summer,
the Marquis of Jìn sent Xún Wú on a courtesy visit.
The Duke met with men of Jìn, Liáng Xiāo of Zhèng, men of Sòng, and men of Cáo at Chányuān.
In autumn,
the Duke of Sòng killed his heir apparent, Cuó.
Men of Jìn seized Nìng Xǐ of Wèi.
This seizure was of a guilty person;
why is it not considered a punitive action by a hegemon?
Because he was not seized for his actual crime.
In the eighth month, on Rénwǔ,
the Baron of Xǔ, Nìng, died in Chǔ.
In winter,
the Viscount of Chǔ, the Marquis of Cài, and the Marquis of Chén attacked Zhèng.
The burial of Lord Líng of Xǔ took place.
In the twenty-seventh year, in spring,
the Marquis of Qí sent Qìng Fēng on a courtesy visit.
In summer,
Shūsūn Bào met with Zhào Wǔ of Jìn, Qū Jiàn of Chǔ, Gōngsūn Guīshēng of Cài, Shí È of Wèi, Kǒng Yuàn of Chén, Liáng Xiāo of Zhèng, men of Xǔ, and men of Cáo in Sòng.
Wèi killed its senior minister Nìng Xǐ,
and the younger brother of the Marquis of Wèi, Zhuān, fled to Jìn.
Wèi killed its senior minister Nìng Xǐ;
then why did the younger brother of the Marquis of Wèi, Zhuān, flee to Jìn?
He fled because of the killing of Nìng Xǐ.
Why did he flee because of the killing of Nìng Xǐ?
Nìng Chí of Wèi and Sūn Línfǔ had expelled the Marquis of Wèi and set up Gōngsūn Piào.
Nìng Chí, falling ill and nearing death,
said to Xǐ:
"The deposing of the Duke was not my intention;
the Sūn family did it.
I am about to die;
can you firmly restore the Duke?"
Xǐ said:
"I will."
After Nìng Chí died,
Xǐ was established as a senior minister.
He sent a man to tell Duke Xiàn:
"The one who deposed you was not the Nìng family;
the Sūn family did it.
I wish to restore you; what do you think?"
Duke Xiàn said:
"If you wish to restore me,
I ask to make a covenant with you."
Xǐ said:
"There is no need for a covenant;
I ask to have the Duke's son Zhuān guarantee it."
Duke Xiàn said to the Duke's son Zhuān:
"The Nìng family is about to restore me;
I wish to make a covenant with them.
They said:
'There is no need for a covenant;
I ask to have the Duke's son Zhuān guarantee it.'
You must make the agreement with them for me."
The Duke's son Zhuān declined, saying:
"To bear the tether and halter,
and follow the ruler east, west, south, and north with axe and block in hand—
these are the duties of a servant or a lesser son.
But to make agreements as a guarantee of good faith—
that is not something a servant or lesser son dares to take part in."
Duke Xiàn angrily said:
"Those who deposed me—
it was not just the Nìng and Sūn families;
it was all because of you."
The Duke's son Zhuān had no choice but to make the agreement with them.
After the agreement was made,
he returned,
and upon arrival,
they killed Nìng Xǐ.
The Duke's son Zhuān took his wife and children and left,
and when about to cross the Yellow River,
he made a covenant with them, carrying his wife and children,
saying:
"If ever I set foot on Wèi territory again,
or eat the grain of Wèi,
may I be blinded like that pheasant."
In autumn, in the seventh month, on Xīnsì,
Bào and the senior ministers of the feudal lords made a covenant in Sòng.
Why is Bào mentioned again?
It is to put the feudal lords in peril.
Why put the feudal lords in peril?
Because Shí È of Wèi was there,
and it is said that the followers of evil men were there.
In winter, in the twelfth month, on the first day, Yǐhài,
there was an eclipse of the sun.
In the twenty-eighth year, in spring,
there was no ice.
In summer,
Shí È of Wèi fled to Jìn.
The Viscount of Zhūlóu came to court.
In autumn, in the eighth month,
a great rain sacrifice was held.
Zhòngsūn Jié went to Jìn.
In winter,
Qí's Qìng Fēng came fleeing here.
In the eleventh month,
the duke went to Chǔ.
In the twelfth month, on the jiǎyín day,
the Son of Heaven passed away.
On the jǐwèi day,
Chǔ's Zǐ Zhāo died.
In the twenty-ninth year, in spring, the king's first month,
the duke was in Chǔ.
Why is it mentioned that the duke was in Chǔ?
It was to record the ruler's presence in the first month.
In summer, in the fifth month,
the duke arrived from Chǔ.
On the gēngwǔ day,
Wèi's Hóu Kàn died.
Yǔ assassinated Wú's Zǐ Yújì.
Who was Yǔ?
He was a gatekeeper,
a punished man.
Why is a punished man called Yǔ?
Because a punished man is not a proper person.
A nobleman does not associate with punished men;
associating with punished men is a path to taking death lightly.
Zhòngsūn Jié met with Jìn's Xún Yíng, Qí's Gāo Zhǐ, Sòng's Huà Dìng, Wèi's Shìshū Qí, Zhèng's Gōngsūn Duàn, and men of Cáo, Jǔ, Zhūlóu, Téng, Xuē, and Xiǎo Zhūlóu to wall Qǐ.
Jìn's Hóu sent Shì Yǎng to come on a friendly mission.
Qǐ's Zǐ came to covenant.
Wú's Zǐ sent Zhá to come on a friendly mission.
Wú had neither a ruler nor great officers;
why here are there a ruler and great officers?
It was to esteem Jìzǐ.
Why esteem Jìzǐ?
For yielding the state.
How did he yield the state?
Yè, Yújì, Yímèi, and Jìzǐ were four brothers sharing the same mother;
Jìzǐ was young and talented,
and his elder brothers all loved him,
all wishing to establish him as ruler.
Yè said:
"If now we urgently give the state to Jìzǐ,
Jìzǐ would still not accept it.
I ask that we not pass it to sons but to brothers,
with us brothers taking turns as rulers,
and then deliver the state to Jìzǐ."
They all said:
"Yes."
Therefore, all those who became rulers
took death lightly and acted bravely,
and when drinking and eating, they would pray,
saying:
"If Heaven desires Wú to have the state,
may it quickly bring regret upon my person."
Thus, when Yè died,
Yújì was established.
When Yújì died,
Yímèi was established.
When Yímèi died,
then the state should have gone to Jìzǐ.
But Jìzǐ was on a mission and absent.
Liáo was the eldest of the concubine-born sons,
and he took the throne.
When Jìzǐ returned from his mission,
he arrived and acknowledged him as ruler.
Hélú said:
"The reason our late ruler did not give the state to his son but to his brother
was entirely for Jìzǐ's sake.
If we follow the late ruler's command,
then the state should go to Jìzǐ;
if we do not follow the late ruler's command,
then I should be established.
How can Liáo become ruler?"
Thereupon, he sent Zhuānzhū to assassinate Liáo,
and delivered the state to Jìzǐ.
Jìzǐ did not accept it, saying:
"You assassinated my ruler,
and if I accept the state from you,
that would make me a co-usurper with you.
You killed my elder brother,
and if I then kill you,
that would be fathers, sons, and brothers killing each other without end."
He left for Yánlíng,
and never entered the capital of Wú again for life.
Therefore, the nobleman regards his not accepting as righteousness,
and his not killing as benevolence.
If Jìzǐ is esteemed, why does Wú have a ruler and great officers?
Because with Jìzǐ as a minister,
there should properly be a ruler.
Who is Zhá?
He is Wú's Jìzǐ's personal name.
The Spring and Autumn Annals does not record the names of the worthy;
why here is the name recorded?
When approving barbarians, one does not do so fully at once.
Jìzǐ is one who is esteemed;
why is Jìzǐ not fully approved?
To approve a man as a minister, one must make him truly ministerial;
to approve a man as a son, one must make him truly filial.
In autumn, in the ninth month,
Wèi Xiàngōng was buried.
Qí's Gāo Zhǐ fled to Běi Yān.
In winter,
Zhòngsūn Jié went to Jìn.
In the thirtieth year, in spring, the king's first month,
Chǔ's Zǐ sent Wěi Pō to come on a friendly mission.
In summer, in the fourth month,
Cài's crown prince Bān assassinated his ruler Gù.
In the fifth month, on the jiǎwǔ day,
there was a fire in Sòng,
and Bó Jī died.
The Son of Heaven killed his younger brother Niánfū.
Prince Xiá fled to Jìn.
In autumn, in the seventh month,
Shū Gōng went to Sòng,
to bury Sòng's Gòng Jī.
The burial of an external lord's wife is not recorded;
why is it recorded here?
To express pity for her.
Why pity her?
There was a fire in Sòng,
and Bó Jī died there.
Why is she referred to by her posthumous title?
Because she was worthy.
Why was she worthy?
When the fire broke out in Sòng,
Bó Jī was present.
The officer in charge reported:
"The fire has arrived;
please come out."
Bó Jī said:
"I cannot.
I have heard that
a woman, when going out at night,
does not descend the hall without seeing her governess and nurse.
The governess has arrived,
but the nurse has not yet arrived."
She was caught by the fire and died.
Zhèng's Liáng Xiāo fled to Xǔ,
and from Xǔ entered Zhèng,
where the people of Zhèng killed Liáng Xiāo.
In winter, in the tenth month,
Cài Jǐnggōng was buried.
The perpetrator had not been punished;
why is the burial recorded?
It is the wording of the nobleman.
Men from Jìn, Qí, Sòng, Wèi, Zhèng, Cáo, Jǔ, Zhūlóu, Téng, Xuē, Qǐ, and Xiǎo Zhūlóu met at Chányuān,
because of the disaster in Sòng.
What is meant by "because of the disaster in Sòng"?
The feudal lords met at Chányuān,
all because of the disaster in Sòng.
Meetings are not usually recorded with their purpose stated;
why is the purpose stated here?
To record (the event in relation to) Bó Jī.
The feudal lords gathered,
and restored what Sòng had lost,
saying, "The dead cannot be brought back to life,
but your wealth can be restored."
This was a major event;
why were minor figures sent?
They were ministers.
If they were ministers, why are they referred to as "men"?
To贬 (demote/criticize).
Why贬?
Because ministers should not be concerned with the affairs of other feudal lords.
In the thirty-first year, in spring, the king's first month.
In summer, in the sixth month, on Xīnsì,
the duke died in the Chǔ palace.
In autumn, in the ninth month, on Guǐsì,
Zǐyě passed away.
On Jǐhài,
Zhòngsūn Jié died.
In winter, in the tenth month,
the viscount of Téng came to attend the burial.
On Guǐyǒu,
we buried our lord, Duke Xiāng.
In the eleventh month,
men from Jǔ assassinated their lord, Mìzhōu.
In the first year, in spring, the king's first month,
the duke ascended the throne.
Shūsūn Bào met with Zhào Wǔ of Jìn, Prince Wéi of Chǔ, Guózhuó of Qí, Xiàngxū of Sòng, Shí'è of Wèi, Prince Zhāo of Chén, Gōngsūn Guīshēng of Cài, Xuānhǔ of Zhèng, and men from Xǔ and Cáo at Huǒ.
This is Zhāo, the younger brother of the marquis of Chén;
why is he not called "younger brother"?
贬.
Why贬?
贬 for killing the heir-apparent Yǎnshī,
it is said, "Zhāo, the younger brother of the marquis of Chén, killed Yǎnshī, the heir-apparent of Chén."
When great officers kill each other, they are referred to as "men";
why here is he referred to by name in the killing?
It indicates that he would from this proceed to assassinate his lord.
Now that he was about to do so,
why is the wording the same as for one who personally assassinated?
For the lord and kin, there should be no "about to";
if "about to," he must be executed.
Then why was he not贬 at the time of the assassination?
Because when a close relative assassinates,
then his crime is especially heinous;
the Spring and Autumn Annals do not wait to贬;
when the crime is evident without being贬 or cut off,
they do not贬 or cut off to show the crime.
When the crime becomes evident only after贬 or cutting off,
then they贬 or cut off to show the crime.
Now Zhāo's crime was already grave;
why贬 again here?
To make clear that Zhāo was guilty.
Why make clear that Zhāo was guilty?
To say that Chǔ used punishing Zhāo as a pretext to destroy Chén.
In the third month, took Yùn.
What is Yùn?
It is a town within (our state).
Why say "took" it?
Because it did not obey.
In summer,
Qián, the younger brother of the earl of Qín, fled to Jìn.
Qín has no great officers;
why is this recorded?
Because he took office in Jìn.
Why did he take office in Jìn?
Having a state of a thousand chariots,
yet unable to accommodate his own maternal brother,
thus the gentleman calls it "fled."
In the sixth month, on Dīngsì,
the viscount of Zhūlóu, Huá, died.
Xún Wú of Jìn led troops and defeated the Dí at Tàiyuán.
This is Dàlǔ;
why call it Tàiyuán?
For geographical features, follow the Central States;
for town and personal names, follow the host.
What is yuán?
Level on high is called yuán;
level below is called xí.
In autumn,
Qùjí of Jǔ entered Jǔ from Qí.
Zhǎn of Jǔ fled to Wú.
Shū Gōng led troops to border the fields of Yùn.
What is "bordering the fields of Yùn"?
It means making a boundary with Jǔ.
Making a boundary with Jǔ,
then why lead troops there?
Out of fear of Jǔ.
Buried Duke Dào of Zhūlóu.
In winter, in the eleventh month, on Jǐyǒu,
Juǎn, the viscount of Chǔ, died.
Bǐ, a prince of Chǔ, fled to Jìn.
In the second year, in spring,
the marquis of Jìn sent Hán Qǐ on a friendly mission.
In summer,
Shū Gōng went to Jìn.
In autumn,
Zhèng killed its great officer Gōngsūn Hēi.
In winter,
the duke went to Jìn,
but upon reaching the river, returned.
What is meant by "upon reaching the river, returned"?
He did not dare to proceed.
Jìsūn Sù went to Jìn.
In the third year, in spring, the king's first month, on Dīngwèi,
Quán, the viscount of Téng, died.
In summer,
Shū Gōng went to Téng.
In the fifth month,
buried Duke Chéng of Téng.
In autumn,
the viscount of Xiǎo Zhūlóu came for an audience.
In the eighth month,
held the great rain sacrifice.
In winter,
there was heavy hail.
Kuǎn, the earl of Běi Yàn, fled to Qí.
In the fourth year, in spring, the king's first month,
there was heavy snow.
In summer,

the viscount of Chǔ, the marquis of Cài, the marquis of Chén, the earl of Zhèng, the baron of Xǔ, the viscount of Xú, the viscount of Téng, the viscount of Dùn, the viscount of Hú, the viscount of Shěn, the viscount of Xiǎo Zhūlóu, the heir-apparent Zuǒ of Sòng, and the Huáiyí met at Shēn.
Men of Chǔ seized the viscount of Xú.
In autumn, in the seventh month,
the viscount of Chǔ, the marquis of Cài, the marquis of Chén, the baron of Xǔ, the viscount of Dùn, the viscount of Hú, the viscount of Shěn, and the Huáiyí attacked Wú,
seized Qìng Fēng of Qí,
and killed him.
This was an attack on Wú;
why mention seizing Qìng Fēng of Qí?
It was to execute for Qí.
How was it executing for Qí?
Qìng Fēng had fled to Wú,
and Wú enfeoffed him at Fáng.
Then why not say they attacked Fáng?

Xún Yǐn and Shì Jíshè of Jìn entered Zhāogē,
and rebelled.
Jìn's Zhào Yǎng returned to Jìn.
This was a rebellion,
why is it said he returned?
Because he used territory to rectify the state.
How did he use territory to rectify the state?
Jìn's Zhào Yǎng took the armor of Jìnyáng to expel Xún Yín and Shì Jíshè.
Who were Xún Yín and Shì Jíshè?
Who were they?
They were the wicked men by the ruler's side.
This expulsion of the wicked men by the ruler's side,
why is it spoken of as a rebellion?
Because it was done without the ruler's command.
Xuè assassinated its ruler Bǐ.
In the fourteenth year, spring,
Wèi's Gōngshū Shù came fleeing.
Jìn's Zhào Yáng fled out to Sòng.
In the second month, on Xīnsì,
Chǔ's prince Jié and Chén's prince Tuórén led troops to destroy Dùn,
and took Dùn's ruler Càng back with them.
In summer,
Wèi's Běigōng Jié came fleeing.
In the fifth month,
Yūyuè defeated Wú at Zuìlǐ.
Wú's ruler Guāng died.
The duke met with the marquis of Qí and the marquis of Wèi at Jiān.
The duke arrived from the meeting.
In autumn,
the marquis of Qí and the duke of Sòng met at Táo.
The Heavenly King sent Shí Shàng to come and present shèn.
Who was Shí Shàng?
He was an officer of the Son of Heaven.
What is shèn?
It is the offering in the sacrificial vessel.
Raw is called shèn,
cooked is called fán.
Wèi's heir apparent Kuǎikuì fled out to Sòng.
Wèi's Gōng Mèng Kōu fled out to Zhèng.
Sòng's duke's younger brother Chén came fleeing from Xiāo.
A great hunt was held at Bǐpú.
The ruler of Zhūlóu came to meet the duke.
The cities of Jǔfǔ and Xiāo were walled.
In the fifteenth year, spring, the royal first month,
the ruler of Zhūlóu came to court.
A field mouse ate the suburban sacrifice ox,
the ox died,
and another ox was divined for.
Why is it not stated what it ate?
Because it was scattered.
In the second month, on Xīnchǒu,
the ruler of Chǔ destroyed Hú,
and took Hú's ruler Bào back with him.
In summer, the fifth month, on Xīnhài,
the suburban sacrifice was held.
Why was the suburban sacrifice held in summer, the fifth month?
Because of the cycle of three divinations.
On Rénshēn,
the duke died in the high寝.
Zhèng's Xuān Dá led troops to attack Sòng.
The marquis of Qí and the marquis of Wèi stationed at Qúchú.
The ruler of Zhūlóu came to rush to the mourning.
Why is it said he came rushing to the mourning?
Rushing to mourning is not according to ritual.
In autumn, the seventh month, on Rénshēn,
Lady Sì died.
Who was Lady Sì?
She was Duke Āi's mother.
Why is she not called consort?
Because Duke Āi had not yet become ruler.
In the eighth month, on the first day Gēngchén,
there was an eclipse of the sun.
In the ninth month,
the ruler of Téng came to attend the burial.
On Dīngsì,
our ruler Duke Dìng was buried.
It rained,
and they could not complete the burial.
On Wǔwǔ,
when the sun was declining,
they then could complete the burial.
On Xīnsì,
Dìng Sì was buried.
Why is the burial of Dìng Sì recorded?
She was a ruler who had not passed the year,
but if she had a son, then there is a temple,
and if there is a temple, then the burial is recorded.
In winter,
the city of Qī was walled.
In the first year, spring, the royal first month,
the duke ascended the throne.
The ruler of Chǔ, the marquis of Chén, the marquis of Suí, and the viscount of Xǔ besieged Cài.
A field mouse ate the suburban sacrifice ox,
and another ox was divined for.
In summer, the fourth month, on Xīnsì,
the suburban sacrifice was held.
In autumn,
the marquis of Qí and the marquis of Wèi attacked Jìn.
In winter,
Zhòngsūn Héjì led troops to attack Zhūlóu.
In the second year, spring, the royal second month,
Jìsūn Sī, Shūsūn Zhōuqiú, and Zhòngsūn Héjì led troops to attack Zhūlóu,
and took the fields east of Kuò and west of Yí.
On Guǐsì,
Shūsūn Zhōuqiú and Zhòngsūn Héjì made a covenant with the ruler of Zhūlóu at Gōuyì.
In summer, the fourth month, on Bǐngzǐ,
the marquis of Wèi, Yuán, died.
The ruler of Téng came to court.
Jìn's Zhào Yǎng led troops to escort Wèi's heir apparent Kuǎikuì into Qī.
What is Qī?
It is a town of Wèi.
Why is it not said he entered Wèi?
Because a father can have a son,
but a son cannot possess his father.
In autumn, the eighth month, on Jiǎxū,
Jìn's Zhào Yǎng led troops and fought with Zhèng's Xuān Dá who led troops at Lì,
and the Zhèng army was badly defeated.
In winter, the tenth month,
Wèi's Duke Líng was buried.
In the eleventh month,
Cài moved to Zhōulái.
Cài killed its great officer prince Sì.
In the third year, in spring,
Guó Xià of Qí and Shí Màngū of Wèi led troops to besiege Qī.
Why did Guó Xià of Qí join Shí Màngū of Wèi in leading troops to besiege Qī?
It was a just punitive expedition by a hegemon.
How was this a just punitive expedition by a hegemon?
Màngū received orders from Duke Líng and established Zhé,
for according to Màngū's duty, it was right to resist him.
Who was Zhé?
He was the son of Kuǎikuì.
Then why was Kuǎikuì not established, but Zhé was?
Kuǎikuì acted without principle,
so Duke Líng expelled Kuǎikuì and established Zhé.
Then, was it right for Zhé to be established?
The reply is:
"Yes."
How was it right?
He did not use his father's command to refuse his grandfather's command,
but used his grandfather's command to refuse his father's command,
thus the father's actions were carried out through the son.
He did not use family affairs to refuse royal affairs,
but used royal affairs to refuse family affairs,
thus the superior's actions were carried out through the inferior.
In summer, on the jiǎwǔ day of the fourth month,
there was an earthquake.
In the fifth month, on the xīnmǎo day,
the temples of Duke Huán and Duke Xī caught fire.
These were both destroyed temples,
why is it recorded as a fire?
They were re-established.
Why is their re-establishment not mentioned?
What the Spring and Autumn Annals has shown once is not shown again.
Why does it not use 'and'?
They were of equal rank.
Why is this recorded?
To record the disaster.
Jìsūn Sī and Shūsūn Zhōuqiú led troops to wall Kāiyáng.
Lè Kūn of Sòng led troops to attack Cáo.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the bǐngzǐ day,
Jìsūn Sī died.
The men of Cài exiled their great officer Gōngsūn Liè to Wú.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the guǐmǎo day,
the Earl of Qín died.
Shūsūn Zhōuqiú and Zhòngsūn Héjì led troops to besiege Zhūlóu.
In the fourth year, in spring, in the king's third month, on the gēngxū day,
a robber killed Cài Hóu Shēn.
When a ruler is assassinated, if the perpetrator is base, he is referred to as 'a man';
why here is he called 'a robber' who assassinated?
He was base among the base.
Who is meant by 'base among the base'?
It means a criminal.
Gōngsūn Chén of Cài fled to Wú.
Duke Huì of Qín was buried.
The men of Sòng seized the ruler of Xiǎozhūlóu.
In summer,
Cài killed its great officers Gōngsūn Guīxìng and Gōngsūn Huò.
The men of Jìn seized the Róngmàn leader,
and Chì returned to Chǔ.
Who was Chì?
He was the name of the Róngmàn leader.
Why does it say he returned to Chǔ?
Master Běigōng said:
"To avoid acknowledging Jìn as hegemon and Chǔ as the capital."
The western outer wall was walled.
In the sixth month, on the xīnchǒu day,
the Pú shrine caught fire.
What was the Pú shrine?
It was the earth-god altar of a perished state.
An earth-god altar is a mound;
why is it recorded as a fire?
The earth-god altar of a perished state is covered over,
its top is covered and its base is fenced with firewood.
Why is the fire at the Pú shrine recorded?
To record the disaster.
In autumn, in the eighth month, on the jiǎyín day,
the Viscount of Téng, Jié, died.
In winter, in the twelfth month,
Duke Zhāo of Cài was buried.
Duke Qǐng of Téng was buried.
In the fifth year, in spring,
Bǐ was walled.
In summer,
the Hóu of Qí attacked Sòng.
Zhào Yǎng of Jìn led troops to attack Wèi.
In autumn, in the ninth month, on the guǐyǒu day,
the Hóu of Qí, Chǔjiù, died.
In winter,
Shū Xuán went to Qí.
In the intercalary month,
Duke Jǐng of Qí was buried.
Intercalary months are not recorded;
why is this one recorded?
Because the mourning period includes the intercalary month in the count.
Why does the mourning period include the intercalary month in the count?
The count for mourning is approximate.
In the sixth year, in spring,
Jiā of Zhūlóu was walled.
Zhào Yǎng of Jìn led troops to attack Xiānyú.
Wú attacked Chén.
In summer,
Guó Xià and Gāo Zhāng of Qí came fleeing.
Shū Xuán met with Wú at Zū.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the gēngyín day,
the Viscount of Chǔ, Zhěn, died.
Yángshēng of Qí entered Qí.
Qí Chén Qǐ assassinated his ruler Shě.
When someone assassinates and sets up another,
it is not expressed with the terminology of controlling the state.
Why here is it expressed with the terminology of controlling the state?
Because of deception.
How was this deception?
Duke Jǐng said to Chén Qǐ:
"I wish to set up Shě, what do you think?"
Chén Qǐ said:
"What pleases one about being a ruler,
is that if you wish to establish someone, then establish them,
if you do not wish to establish them, then do not.
If you, my lord, wish to establish him,
then I, your minister, request to establish him."
Yángshēng said to Chén Qǐ:
"I hear that you probably do not wish to establish me."
Chén Qǐ said:
"The lord of a thousand chariots,
when about to depose the rightful heir and establish the unrightful,
must kill the rightful one.
My not establishing you,
is the means to preserve your life.
Flee!"
He gave him a jade tally and helped him escape.
Duke Jǐng died and Shě was established.
Chén Qǐ sent men to welcome Yángshēng,
and placed him among his household.
After the mourning for Duke Jǐng was concluded,
all the great officers were at court.
Chén Qǐ said:
"Cháng's mother has a fish and bean sacrifice,
I hope the great officers will grace me."
The great officers all said:
"Yes."
Thereupon they all went to Chén Qǐ's home,
and sat down.
Chén Qǐ said:
"I have some armor,
I beg to show it."
The great officers all said:
"Yes."
Thereupon he had strong men lift a large sack to the central courtyard.
When the great officers saw it,
they all turned pale with shock.
Opening it,
there was Gōngzǐ Yángshēng revealed.
Chén Qǐ said:
"This is your ruler!"
The great officers had no alternative,
all hesitantly faced north, bowed twice, touched their heads to the ground, and acknowledged him as ruler.
From this they went and assassinated Shě.
Winter,
Zhòngsūn Héjì led troops to attack Zhūlóu.
Sòng Xiàng Cháo led troops to attack Cáo.
Seventh year, spring,
Sòng Huáng Yuàn led troops to invade Zhèng.
Jìn Wèi Mànduō led troops to invade Wèi.
Summer,
the duke met with Wú at Zēng.
Autumn,
the duke attacked Zhūlóu.
Eighth month, Jǐyǒu day,
entered Zhūlóu,
and brought Zhūlóuzǐ Yì back.
Entry is not mentioned with attack,
why here is attack mentioned?
It is an internal expression,
as if done by others.
Why is Zhūlóuzǐ Yì named?
Cut off.
Why cut off?
Captured.
Why not mention his capture?
To conceal great internal evil.
Sòng men besieged Cáo.
Winter,
Zhèng Sì Hóng led troops to rescue Cáo.
Eighth year, spring, royal first month,
the Duke of Sòng entered Cáo,
and took Cáobó Yáng back.
Why is Cáobó Yáng named?
Cut off.
Why cut off?
Annulled.
Why not mention its annihilation?
To conceal the annihilation of a same-surname state.
Why conceal the annihilation of a same-surname state?
Because they had the power to save it but did not save it.
Wú attacked us.
Summer,
Qí men took Huān and Dàn.
External taking of towns is not recorded,
why here is it recorded?
Because they were bribing Qí.
Why bribe Qí?
Because they had brought Zhūlóuzǐ Yì back.
Returned Zhūlóuzǐ Yì to Zhūlóu.
Autumn, seventh month.
Winter, twelfth month, Guǐhài day,
Qǐbó Guò died.
Qí men returned Huān and Dàn.
Ninth year, spring, royal second month,
buried Qǐ Xīgōng.
Sòng Huáng Yuàn led troops and took the Zhèng army at Yōngqiū.
Why say "took" them?
Easy.
How was it easy?
By deception.
Summer,
Chǔ men attacked Chén.
Autumn,
the Duke of Sòng attacked Zhèng.
Winter, tenth month.
Tenth year, spring, royal second month,
Zhūlóuzǐ Yì came fleeing.
The duke joined Wú in attacking Qí.
Third month, Wùxū day,
Qíhóu Yángshēng died.
Summer,
Sòng men attacked Zhèng.
Jìn Zhào Yāng led troops to invade Qí.
Fifth month,
the duke arrived from attacking Qí.
Buried Qí Dàogōng.
Wèi Gōngmèng Kōu returned from Qí to Wèi.
Xuébó Yín died.
Autumn,
buried Xuē Huìgōng.
Winter,
Chǔ Gōngzǐ Jié led troops to attack Chén.
Wú rescued Chén.
Eleventh year, spring,
Qí Guó Shū led troops to attack us.
Summer,
Chén Yuán Pō fled to Zhèng.
Fifth month,
the duke joined Wú in attacking Qí.
Jiǎxū day,
Qí Guó Shū led troops and battled Wú at Àilíng,
the Qí army was defeated,
and Qí Guó Shū was captured.
Autumn, seventh month, Xīnyǒu day,
Téngzǐ Yǔmǔ died.
Winter, eleventh month,
buried Téng Yǐngōng.
Wèi Shìshū Qí fled to Sòng.
In the twelfth year, in spring,
the land tax was implemented.
Why is this recorded?
To criticize.
What is criticized?
It criticizes the beginning of the land tax.
In summer, on the jiachen day of the fifth month,
Mèngzǐ passed away.
Who was Mèngzǐ?
She was the wife of Duke Zhāo.
Why is she referred to as Mèngzǐ?
To conceal the marriage to someone of the same surname,
as she was a woman from Wú.
The duke met with Wú at Tuógāo.
In autumn,
the duke met with the Marquis of Wèi and Huáng Yuàn of Sòng at Yùn.
Xiàng Cháo of Sòng led troops to attack Zhèng.
In winter, in the twelfth month,
there were locusts.
Why is this recorded?
To record an anomaly.
What was anomalous?
It was out of season.
In the thirteenth year, in spring,
Xuān Dá of Zhèng led troops to capture the Sòng army at Yán.
Why does it say "capture"?
Because it was easy.
How was it easy?
It was through a deceptive reversal.
In summer,
Xǔ's Earl Wù passed away.
The duke met with the Marquis of Jìn and the Viscount of Wú at Huángchí.
Why is Wú referred to as "Viscount"?
Because Wú presided over the meeting.
If Wú presided, why is the Marquis of Jìn mentioned first?
Because we do not acknowledge the Yí Dí presiding over the central states.
Why does it say "and the Viscount of Wú"?
It is the wording for a meeting of two leaders.
If we do not acknowledge the Yí Dí presiding over the central states,
then why use the wording for a meeting of two leaders?
To honor Wú.
Why honor Wú?
Because with Wú present, no feudal lord under heaven dared not attend.
Chǔ's Gōngzǐ Shēn led troops to attack Chén.
Yúyuè invaded Wú.
In autumn,
the duke returned from the meeting.
Jìn's Wèi Duō led troops to invade Wèi.
This is Jìn's Wèi Mànduō.
Why is he called Jìn's Wèi Duō?
To criticize the use of two names,
as two names are contrary to ritual.
The burial of Duke Yuán of Xǔ took place.
In the ninth month,
there were locusts.
In winter, in the eleventh month,
a comet appeared in the east.
What is a "comet"?
It is a broom star.
Why does it say "in the east"?
Because it appeared at dawn.
Why is this recorded?
To record an anomaly.
Bandits killed Xià Ōufū of Chén.
In the twelfth month,
there were locusts.
In the fourteenth year, in spring,
a qílín was captured during a western hunt.
Why is this recorded?
To record an anomaly.
What was anomalous?
It was not a beast of the central states.
Then who hunted it?
It was a firewood gatherer.
A firewood gatherer is a humble person;
why use the term "hunt"?
To elevate it.
Why elevate it?
Because the capture of the qílín was significant.
Why was the capture of the qílín significant?
The qílín is a beast of benevolence.
It appears when there is a true king,
and does not appear when there is none.
Someone reported, saying:
"There is a stag-like creature with horns."
Confucius said:
"For whom has it come?
For whom has it come?"
He turned his sleeve to wipe his face,
and tears soaked his robe.
When Yán Yuān died,
the Master said:
"Alas!
Heaven is destroying me."
When Zǐlù died,
the Master said:
"Alas! Heaven is cursing me."
When the qílín was captured in the western hunt,
Confucius said:
"My way has come to an end."
Why does the Spring and Autumn Annals begin with Duke Yǐn?
Because it is what the ancestors have passed down as heard.
What was seen is recorded with different wording,
what was heard is recorded with different wording,
and what was transmitted is recorded with different wording.
Why does it end in the fourteenth year of Duke Āi?
It is said:
"It is complete!"
Why did the nobleman compile the Spring and Autumn Annals?
To bring order to a chaotic age,
and return to the right path—
nothing comes closer than the Spring and Autumn Annals.
Is it not known whether this is so?
Or is it that the nobleman delighted in the Way of Yáo and Shùn?
Is it not also that he delighted in Yáo and Shùn's recognition of the nobleman?
He established the principles of the Spring and Autumn Annals to await later sages,
for the nobleman's actions also found joy in this.
